Pay the one red of hosted run 35606210194 (R2779's tip), open-debt item 810,
and build the gate its class should have had after the first time.

THE RED, READ FROM ITS BODY. Layer C1's workspace test failed one test:
wz-replay's `the_alert_reaches_a_peer_and_a_clean_capture_sends_it_nothing`,
at "a complete capture must not even dial" -- a listener that must stay quiet
accepted a connection. Read against the code rather than rerun into green: a
second test in the same binary, run in parallel, took its unreachable
destination by binding a port, reading the number and RELEASING it, then
dialled it with retries. The kernel hands a released number to the next
`bind(:0)`, and the quiet listener's was next.

IT IS ITEM 806 AGAIN, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. R2778 repaid 806 with one
shared helper, `refusing_port` (hold a bound, never-listening socket), and a
sweep for the other shape. The sweep was a search framed around three
consumer crates; wz-replay was a fourth, and the site that reded here is one
the sweep did not reach. A class that leaks twice gets a gate.

THE GATE DERIVES ITS POPULATION; THE SEARCH DID NOT. `released_port_gate.py`
reads tracked crates/**.rs through the shared comment scanner (now able to
blank literal bodies, so a brace in a format string cannot move a scope) and
finds every socket number that outlives its socket, in three shapes: a
temporary that a bind produced, an explicit drop with the number still used
after, and a scope that ends while the number leaves it -- through the tail,
a return, or a `let` that reaches either -- including when the number came
from a helper returning (socket, address), which is how R2778's own note had
called a listen picker. Each site is classified from a closed set
(listen-picker, not-a-port, bind-probe, held-elsewhere) with a reason; an
unclassified site, a row naming no site and an empty population all FAIL.
There is no class for a dial target that must refuse: that has one correct
shape, and a released number used for it is the defect.

IT FOUND ONE MORE. A reconnect test killed its peer by dropping the listener
and revived it by binding the same address again -- the drop freed the
number, so a neighbour could answer the dials that must be refused, or take
the number and fail the rebind. It needed a shape the helper did not have:
the number held while a listener comes and goes. `refusing_port` now sets
SO_REUSEPORT and offers `listen()`, which shares the held number; a plain
bind still fails, so its reservation is unchanged. Both dial-target sites
hold their number now, and the remaining seven are classified.

The cookie's HEAD -- the peer's zid, role and sizing caps -- is let go
after InitAck and put back from the cookie at OpenSyn: the third of the
four states session-unicast-accept's stateless clause names after R2777's
recount. Building it found a defect in the seam around it, in both roles,
and the defect is paid here because it is the same seam.

THE HEAD, BY ONE WRITER. The four slots it lives in (the accept-side zid,
the routing zid -- the same value twice -- the role, and the caps) are
written together by `install_accept_head`: `None` at the InitAck release,
the carried head at the OpenSyn restore. The caps come back through the
decoder the InitSyn went through, from the byte the peer sent, so the
restored value is the held one exactly. `cookie_valid`'s zid comparison
goes: its own note called it TRANSITIONAL until "the round the held slots
go", and with no held copy there is nothing to compare, which is upstream's
position -- its check has the cookie and the nonce, nothing else.

THE SEED HAD TO MOVE, AND MOVING IT SHOWED WHAT WAS WRONG WITH ITS PLACE.
The acceptor's RX SN seed ran at PARSE time and reads the negotiated ring,
which is the peer's caps -- now absent until the restore. Moving it behind
the restore is upstream's order: `recv_open_syn` checks the nonce, rebuilds
from the cookie, and only then takes the OpenSyn's lease and initial_sn.
But the parse step also applied the seed and the lease to ANY OpenSyn,
admitted or not, and the admission itself never spent its nonce. MEASURED
through the drive: after Established, a replay of the admitting OpenSyn was
admitted again, reset the RX baseline, and a frame the session had already
delivered was delivered a second time. So everything an admitted OpenSyn
does now lives in `admit_open_syn`, after admission and in upstream's
order -- restore, spend the nonce, seed, lease -- and the parse step takes
only the cookie the admission predicate reads.

THE INITIATOR HAD THE SAME SHAPE. Its parse step applied every OpenAck's
initial_sn and lease, and a replayed OpenAck after Established was measured
to do the same thing: baseline reset, duplicate delivered. The class is "an
Open frame's side effects applied outside the handshake that awaits it",
and the population is both roles, not the one the atom names. The
initiator now admits only the one OpenAck its OpenSyn awaits
(`awaiting_open_ack`, set by the OpenSyn send, read by the admission
predicate, cleared by `admit_open_ack`, and by a reopen). That is
session-unicast-open's code; its grade (COMPLETE) is not changed by a
defect found and repaired in the same round, and the correction is this
entry.

Round 2783.decision_summary:
The multilink accept state rides the accept cookie: the last of the four
states session-unicast-accept's stateless clause names after R2777's
recount (auth R2779, region R2780, head R2782).

UPSTREAM'S STATE IS A PAIR BEHIND AN OPTION. Its multilink `StateAccept` is
`Option<(pubkey::StateAccept, ZPublicKey)>`: the challenge it issued and the
initiator's ephemeral key, or nothing when multilink is off. It keeps the
key where its auth-plane pubkey state does not because a multilink link is
bound to its session by that key AFTER OpenSyn. wz's `MultilinkAcceptState`
is the same pair; the `None` arm is also the dispatch's "disabled" flag,
which is the same fact.

IT IS THE COOKIE'S ONE VARIABLE MEMBER, AND THAT DECIDES WHERE IT SITS. The
group of extension states is fixed-width by contract, which is what bounds a
cookie for a no-alloc peer; a public key's encoding is not. So the member is
a self-delimiting tail after the group -- one byte for `None`, `1 ‖ challenge
‖ len ‖ key` for `Some` -- rather than at upstream's position between qos and
shm. The order was wz's own and was followed only while nothing forced it.
The bound still holds where it must, and structurally: offering multilink
takes `transport-multilink`, which implies `session-extauth`, which implies
`alloc`, the profile whose cookie carrier is unbounded; a no-alloc peer
cannot offer it, so every cookie it can be handed has the one-byte `None`.
The widest-cookie test says so and bounds that cookie.

THE DRAW HAD TO MOVE, FOR THE REASON R2779 MOVED THE AUTH ONES. The AP seam
drew the 0x4 challenge once, when it installed the dispatch. With the
release dropping the challenge after InitAck, a second handshake on the same
bundle would have had none to issue. The session now draws it at InitAck
from the bundle's installed entropy source; `refresh_multilink_challenge_
nonce` and the seam's draw are gone, and with them the last constructor of
`OpenError::AuthEntropy`, which is removed rather than left unconstructible.

ONE WRITER EACH WAY, ORDERED. The mint reads the dispatch's state; the
InitAck release returns the dispatch to its offer and clears the key already
latched for the aggregation join; the OpenSyn restore puts the key back and
then the challenge, before the 0x4 stage checks against them, and the join
latch is re-taken from the restored key after that stage. A key that does
not read back leaves no challenge outstanding, so the OpenSyn stage refuses
rather than skipping the check.

THE GRADE STAYS PARTIAL. Every state upstream's cookie struct names is now
carried, but the count that says so was taken by hand and was short twice;
the grade moves when a gate derives it from the struct.

config write, the validator that refuses a bad write -- needs the same two
things first: the document read the way upstream reads it, and the
difference between two documents. wz had neither. Building a consumer first
would have put a second, private reading of the document inside it.

THE SEMANTICS ARE UPSTREAM'S, READ AT THE PIN, NOT INFERRED.
- The reader follows PluginConfig::try_from, VolumeConfig::try_from and
  StorageConfig::try_from field by field, in their order, so the first
  refusal is upstream's first refusal. A present null is not an absence
  there; each arm decides, and `replication: null` enabling replication
  with defaults is reproduced rather than tidied.
- serde_json is built without preserve_order at the pin (its lockfile entry
  carries no indexmap), so upstream's Map is a BTreeMap: storages and
  volumes are visited in NAME order and a repeated key keeps its LAST
  value. Every object read here goes through that shape.
- Equality decides whether a storage RESTARTS, and a restarted memory
  storage has lost its data, so it is upstream's exactly: a storage
  compares every field with its volume payload compared as serde_json
  values (key order not semantic, an integer not the float of its value);
  a volume compares name, paths and rest only, so `__required__` alone is
  no change while `backend` is one (it stays in rest).
- The diff is ConfigDiff::diffs: deleted storages, deleted volumes, added
  volumes, added storages; a changed entry is its delete and its add.
- A key expression must already BE canon (keyexpr::new refuses `**/*`,
  `**/**` and a lone `$*` rather than rewriting them), tested as
  "canonicalises to itself" in the zenoh-c dialect.

WHERE WZ DEPARTS. Two upstream PANICS become refusals: a negative
replication interval (Duration::from_secs_f64) and a propagation delay
beyond the interval (a Duration subtraction). A config value must not be
able to take a node down.

UPSTREAM'S RUNNING PLUGIN, MAPPED ONTO THE MANAGER WZ HAS.
- Start is upstream's StorageRuntimeInner::new: the `memory` volume, then
  each declared volume, then each declared storage; a failing step is
  reported and the rest still run ("Failure of loading of one volume or
  storage should not affect others").
- A change is upstream's config_checker: parse the old and the new
  document, apply ConfigDiff::diffs through `update` -- in order, stopping
  at the first failure -- and refuse the write if any step fails. What
  applied before the failure stays applied, because upstream's loop returns
  at its first `?` and a torn-down memory storage cannot be put back with
  its data; the section keeps the old document, so the next write retries.
- A changed volume takes its storages with it (upstream's kill_volume), and
  an unchanged storage on it is not re-created -- upstream's behaviour,
  reproduced and stated rather than repaired.
- The notification plane starts the plugin when its document appears and
  stops it when it goes; stopping removes what the DOCUMENT declared and
  the `memory` volume, and leaves what a client added through the intent
  verbs, because here the plugin shares its manager with them.
- `memory` becomes a backend name (upstream's MEMORY_BACKEND_NAME), and a
  declared volume's `backend` key is kept out of the parameters it is built
  from; a volume with `__path__` is loaded from the first path that loads,
  as upstream loads a plugin declared by paths, or refused by name on a
  build without dynamic volume loading.

ONE DEPARTURE. Upstream refuses to start the storage manager without
`timestamping`, because a stored sample needs a timestamp and only an HLC
session can mint one. A wz storage stamps an unstamped sample itself, so the
precondition holds by construction and no refusal is made.

not Send), so a `plugins/...` write is stashed and applied in the dispatch
closure, through the config's own write gate with the manager as its sink
-- no second copy of the merge, the validator or the notification.

Round 2791.decision_summary:
Honour `bind` and `dscp` on the UDP multicast path, at the surface that
generated their absence rather than at the two sockets that showed it.

`transport-link-udp` is PARTIAL, and one of its residual clauses says
upstream's multicast link reads `bind` and `dscp` while wz's multicast
sockets apply neither. Re-measured before acting, against the pin: it
holds, and the cause is one line older than the sockets. wz derived the
multicast option surface from the keys the udp crate DECLARES -- its own
`pub mod config` is `iface` / `join` / `ttl`, and `McastSocketConfig`'s
doc cites exactly that list -- while `bind` and `dscp` are declared a
crate away in `zenoh-link-commons` and pulled off the endpoint config by
the multicast manager beside the other three. So the surface had no field
for either key: the locator parsed both, `LinkSocketOptions` carried both,
and the one call site that built `McastGroupOptions` read `.iface` and
dropped them. No caller could pass one and no reader could miss one.

That is the base taken here. The alternative -- setting the two options
inside the two constructors -- would leave the surface still three keys
wide and the next key to arrive would go the same way.

The two halves are NOT treated alike, and that asymmetry is upstream's.
Upstream binds and marks its `ucast_sock`, the sending half, and does
neither to the wildcard-bound `mcast_sock` it joins and reads on. wz
splits the roles differently: `bind_multicast_tx` is the pure egress half
and takes both keys, while `bind_multicast` both joins and sends, so it
takes `dscp` -- the same reason the hop limit is already set on it -- and
NOT `bind`, because a socket bound to a unicast address cannot receive the
group at all.

`LinkSocket::resolve` was deliberately not reused for the bind. Its
`LinkSide` is `Dial` or `Listen` and a multicast sending half is neither;
more concretely, the dial path resolves `bind` through a name lookup and
refuses `iface` alongside it, and upstream's multicast path does neither
-- it parses a literal address and lets the two keys compose. Reusing it
would have imported a refusal and a resolver zenoh does not have here.
What IS shared is the one place a DSCP reaches a socket, now named
`apply_dscp`, which `LinkSocket::configure` also calls.

Round 2795.decision_summary:
Split `InterceptorLink` into the two axes it was carrying -- open-debt item
814 -- because one enum was answering two questions that have different
answers for the same link.

A RULE asks which protocol a link is. Upstream answers that off the link's
auth id and files its QUIC datagram link under `quic`, since that link
carries the same `LinkAuthId::Quic` the stream link does. The LINK answers
for itself whether it is streamed, whether it is reliable, and how it
advertises itself, and there the datagram link differs from its stream
sibling. wz's enum held a tenth value, `QuicDatagram`, justified in its doc by
"zenoh has no such transport" -- it has one -- so a rule narrowed to `quic`
governed zenoh's datagram link and missed wz's. For a deny rule that is a
bypass. And wz accepted a `quic-datagram` rule that zenohd refuses.

and rejected: the C snapshot copies its value off the ACL subject and answers
zenoh-c's `z_link_is_streamed` / `z_link_reliability` from it, so that line
would have closed the bypass and made zenoh-c call a datagram link streamed
and reliable. So the axes are now two types. `InterceptorLink` is exactly
upstream's nine. `LinkKind` carries the link's own answers and
`interceptor_protocol()`. `LinkSubject` stores the kind and derives the
protocol, so the two cannot drift; the C snapshot reads the kind.

Round 2796.decision_summary:
Correct a claim this workspace's own record made twice, before anything is
built on it: upstream's reliable UDP is PLAINTEXT QUIC on the wire.

`transport-link-udp`'s last base is the reliable UDP variant, and before
building it I read the upstream module that implements `.security(false)`
rather than the call sites that select it. That file is `plaintext.rs`. The
TLS 1.3 handshake still runs -- a self-signed server certificate, a client
that trusts any -- but only to negotiate the connection. Every level of packet
protection is then replaced by no-op keys: Initial, Handshake, 1-RTT and early.
Encrypt does nothing, decrypt accepts anything, the AEAD tag is zero bytes and
header protection is off.

which is not plaintext"), and R2792's carry repeated it. Both were inferred

Round 2799.decision_summary:
R2797 shipped a door and a revision bump, and the header told a consumer how
to compare the revision PAIR -- the macro they compiled against against the
function the loaded library answers -- which detects a build linked to a
library it was not compiled for. That check is correct for the question it
asks.

It is the wrong shape for a DIFFERENT question, and a consumer asked that one
within the hour: "do we check that wz_capi_c_abi_version() returns 2 before
calling the predicate?" The header said nothing either way, so reading the
only comparison it shows as a feature probe was the reasonable inference.

DECIDED: a single door is tested by RESOLVING ITS SYMBOL, and the revision is
what EXPLAINS an absence afterwards. The argument is not a preference:

  * `== N` refuses a later library that still carries the door, because the
    revision moves on any symbol-set change;
  * `>= N` survives a REMOVAL, which the pin's own refusal text names as an
    ABI event, so it leaves the number above N with the door gone;
  * neither comparison observes the artifact at all. A resolved symbol does.

This is the same distinction this repository already applies to itself and had
not written down for its callers. `capi_c_abi_pin.py` reads the symbol SET out
of the BUILT library and the number by CALLING it, and holds the two against
each other rather than inferring either from the other; the header now points
at that gate as the worked example rather than only as the thing that keeps
the number honest.

The answer was already given to the consumer in a message. That is why this
round exists: a fact that lives only in a message is one the NEXT reader of
this header does not have, and the header is the contract.

Round 2800.decision_summary:
Make the storage read seam hand out values and admit failure, and make the
service above it treat the medium as something that can hold data the gate
never saw. This is the first round of building `storage-backend-filesystem`
to the directory-tree shape the owner chose, and it builds the base that
shape stands on rather than the backend itself.

PROVENANCE. The code was written by this loop's previous run, which stopped
before it committed: it left the diff uncommitted in a linked worktree with
its session-core tests green and three control probes run. This session took
the diff over and did not inherit its verdicts -- every claim below was
re-measured here, on the main worktree, after the diff was applied to it.
Two witnesses were added and one was repaired, for reasons given below.

THE BASE, measured before choosing it. The filesystem backend keeps a full
in-memory mirror of its directory, and its own module doc says why: the
seam's `get` answered `Option<&StoredData>`, a reference, and a reference
can only point at something the backend OWNS. So the mirror was not a
design choice of that backend; the seam generated it, and the dynamic
volume carries the same mirror for the same reason. A mirror loaded at open
serves the directory as it stood then. Upstream's backend reads the file on
every get, so a file changed or dropped into the directory is served as it
is now. No change inside the filesystem backend could express that while
the seam demanded a borrow, which is why the seam is where this starts.

DECIDED, first: `get` answers upstream's shape
(`plugins/zenoh-backend-traits/src/lib.rs` @ `) -> ZResult<Vec<StoredData>>;`)
-- every live version, by value, or a refusal from the medium. It replaces
the old pair (`get` for one borrowed value, `get_versions` for the borrowed
list); `get_newest` is derived from it, so a backend implements one read and
the two cannot disagree. `get_all_entries` answers `Result` too. The error
type is new and payload-free for the reasons the write error already gives.
An absent key is `Ok` with nothing in it: upstream's memory backend answers
`Err` there and its filesystem backend the empty `Ok`, and its service
treats both alike, so wz takes the answer that does not call an absence a
failure.

DECIDED, second: the service does what upstream's storage manager does with
a medium that already holds data, in three places that had no counterpart,
each read at the pin rather than recalled. (1) Hydration: the gate seeds its
newer-wins record from the listing when it opens, every entry a Put, and
FAILS when the listing fails, as upstream bails out of creating the storage
(`plugins/zenoh-plugin-storage-manager/src/storages_mgt/mod.rs` @ `let mut entries = match storage.get_all_entries().await {`);
the tokio service surfaces that as a new `BackendUnreadable` refusal. (2)
The gate's second arm: a key with no record is compared against what the
backend holds, as upstream's cache guard falls back to the storage
(`plugins/zenoh-plugin-storage-manager/src/storages_mgt/service.rs` @ `if let Ok(stored_data) = storage.get(new_event.stripped_key.clone(), "").await {`);
hydration covers what was there at open, this covers what arrived after. A
read the backend refuses is accepted, as upstream's `if let Ok` does. (3)
The non-wildcard query reads its own key, upstream's second reply arm; wz
walked the listing for every query, which for a directory is a walk per
exact get.

DECIDED, third: the newer-wins record carries each event's KIND. The aligner
used to re-derive Put/Delete by asking the backend whether it still held the
key -- a read of every stored value per alignment for a disk, and an answer
to the wrong question: what the medium holds NOW, where the record's subject
is what this storage ACCEPTED. Upstream's record holds the event with its
action. The consequence this session measured is not only cost: a value that
vanished from the medium was advertised as a Delete nobody issued, at the
Put's timestamp, which an aligning peer would apply to its own copy.

TWO WITNESSES THIS SESSION ADDED, because a control would have come back
green without them. The kind decision had no test that could tell the two
derivations apart; one was written (a value the medium lost is still the
accepted Put, and an accepted Delete is still a Delete, in one fixture).
The wildcard update's new refusal arm -- a medium that cannot list reaches
no key -- had none either; one was written (the update is reported and stays
registered, so an older concrete put is still overridden). And one inherited
test was REPAIRED rather than kept: "a query is answered without the key the
medium cannot read" used a fixture that refused EVERY read, so it had one
key and could not show that the others are still answered. The fixture now
refuses one named key, and the test holds two.

ONE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE BEYOND COST, named rather than hidden: a STORED key that
is itself a wildcard (only possible with the wildcard-update registries
compiled out) intersects an exact query, so the listing arm replied it; the
direct arm, like upstream, does not.

ONE DIVERGENCE KEPT AND NAMED: when a wildcard update cannot list its keys,
upstream warns and reports the sample processed; wz reports it as an
uncommitted write, the same answer every other uncommitted write in the gate
gives. Both keep the registration, which is the half a later sample is
judged against, and the witness pins that half too.

Round 2801.decision_summary:
Rebuild `storage-backend-filesystem`'s backend on the directory-tree shape the
owner chose at R2573, with its metadata in upstream's own on-disk format, and
repair the lifetime defect that format's lock exposed one layer up. Second
round of building this atom; it stays PARTIAL.

THE BASE. R2800 removed what generated the old backend's in-memory mirror (a
seam that answered a borrow) and named the next base: the backend itself. The
backend now keeps no copy: a value is a raw file at its key's path, every get
opens that file, and a listing walks the tree under upstream's admission rule --
the trimmed relative path must pass upstream's `keyexpr::new` and intersect
`**`. The rule is PORTED
(`commons/zenoh-keyexpr/src/key_expr/borrowed.rs` @ `impl<'a> TryFrom<&'a str> for &'a keyexpr {`)
rather than borrowed from wz's canonizer, because that one bounds its output at
256 bytes and a file several directories deep is a longer key with nothing
wrong with it.

THE FORMAT, derived rather than chosen. A raw file cannot carry its encoding or
its timestamp; upstream keeps both in `.zenoh_datainfo`, a RocksDB database
beside the files, keyed by the file's path, valued by zenoh-ext's serialization
of `(u64, [u8; 16], u16, Vec<u8>)`
(`zenoh-ext/src/serialization.rs` @ `macro_rules! impl_num {`). The owner's
decision was full parity of the shape, and a directory is only a mirror of the
key space if either implementation can serve what the other wrote. A wz-native
sidecar would reopen a zenohd-written directory with every timestamp replaced
by a file time -- newer than the peers' copies, which alignment never corrects
-- and the name could not be reused with another format, because zenohd opens
whatever sits there as RocksDB and refuses the storage when it cannot. So the
sidecar IS that database: the engine is upstream's pin (rocksdb 0.23.0,
librocksdb-sys held at =0.17.1, RocksDB 9.9.3).

A PREMISE THIS ROUND WROTE AND THEN REFUTED, recorded because it had already
reached a commit message and a manifest comment. The first cut kept rocksdb's
five default codecs "because a reader lacking the codec a sidecar was written
with cannot open it". True of a reader, false of this writer: upstream opens
with `DB::open_default`, which leaves RocksDB's default `compression`, and that
is snappy when snappy is compiled in (the `ColumnFamilyOptions` constructor in
the RocksDB source librocksdb-sys 0.17.1 vendors, read there); the fs backend
configures nothing else. Snappy is the one codec a zenohd-written
sidecar can hold. The other four brought three system-library probes (zlib,
bzip2, zstd via pkg-config) that the apt-package census refused, for blocks
upstream never writes. The dependency now takes snappy alone.

MIRRORED at upstream's definitions: the conflict suffix both ways (a shorter
key's file moves aside WITH its row; a key whose own path is a directory takes
the suffixed name), `@root` for the mount-point key, emptied directories pruned
on delete, the mime_guess fallback for a file with no row and its modification
time stamped with id [1], and `follow_links` / `keep_mime_types` at upstream's
defaults.

DIVERGENCES, each in the safe or stronger direction and each named where it
lives: payload to a staging file, fsync, rename, directory fsync, rows written
with sync, where upstream truncates in place and syncs nothing; payload before
row, so an unconfirmed write keeps the OLDER timestamp and alignment converges;
a delete removes EVERY file holding the key, where upstream removes one and the
older conflict-named value comes back; a key that is not a key expression, or
would alias `@root` or land in the sidecar or staging area, is refused; with
`follow_links` off a write through a link is refused instead of landing outside
the tree unreadable; a linked base directory lists, where upstream serves its
files by key and lists none.

THE LIFETIME DEFECT. The sidecar's lock makes one-store-per-directory enforced
instead of documented, and enforcing it exposed that the garbage collector and
the digest publisher held the storage state STRONGLY from tasks whose `abort`
the runtime processes later, on its own thread. A removed storage's backend
outlived its owner by an unbounded moment. Both now hold it weakly and end when
it is gone. The aligner pull keeps a strong reference: it is a bounded job that
finishes by itself.

R2573's REFUTED PROPERTY. It pinned "a real key ending in the suffix trims to a
different key" as a shape upstream shares. No key can end in `.##z`: `#` is
forbidden in a key expression, which is why upstream trims before it validates.
The residue was wz's alone -- its seam takes a bare string -- and the backend now
refuses a key that is not a key expression.

A GATE POPULATION THIS ROUND'S DEPENDENCY EXPOSED. Even with snappy alone,
`rocksdb` turns on `librocksdb-sys/static`, which is
`["libz-sys?/static", "bzip2-sys?/static"]` -- weak features that activate
nothing -- and `cargo metadata --all-features` still reports
`librocksdb-sys -> libz-sys` and `-> bzip2-sys` in its resolve graph, because
that graph is the lock-level resolve. `cargo tree -i libz-sys --all-features`
prints nothing: no build compiles it. Two gates read the metadata as "what the
build demands": the apt-package census asked every CI job to install zlib and
bzip2 development packages, and the prose build-closure gate took `libz-sys`'s
`links = "z"` into its vocabulary and read `z_id_to_string` in a doc comment as
a claim about libz. Installing the packages would have been a workaround -- a
CI image carrying libraries nothing compiles so a gate could keep a population
it had defined wrongly. The fix is the population: `scripts/lib/cargo_activation.py`
states cargo's own rule (an optional edge is active only when an enabled
feature names `dep:x`, `x` or `x/feat`, never `x?/feat`), with a selftest whose
control -- treating the weak form as activating -- reds it, and both gates now
read activated packages only. Both went green with their populations non-zero
(1 pkg-config module over 107 job pairs; 10 build-script and 2 closure claims).

`Volume::create_storage` takes the config `&mut`, as upstream's takes it by

refutes. The canonical spelling is part of the format: rows are keyed by the

Round 2803.decision_summary:
A consumer reported that a lowlatency capture is unreadable past its
handshake. Measured through this repository's own pcap door: their capture
yielded 4 messages -- the Init and Open of both directions -- against 99 for
a control differing only by `--lowlatency` on both ends. Every drop counter
read zero, so the door reported a clean run while abandoning 20,689 of the
opener's 20,752 stream bytes.

DECIDED: the credible-header gate asks a DIFFERENT QUESTION on a lean link,
because a lean link carries a different message set.

The gate exists to refuse a boundary a stream reader must not resume on, and
it asked `is_credible_transport_header`. Upstream's lowlatency link does not
carry the universal set: `TransportBodyLowLatency` is
`Close | KeepAlive | Network(NetworkMessage)`, so its data-carrying frames are
network messages with no `Frame` wrapper and no sequence number. A network MID
is `0x19..=0x1F` and no transport MID is, so the gate answered "implausible"
for every one of them -- correctly, for the question it was asked.

  `commons/zenoh-protocol/src/transport/mod.rs` @ `pub enum TransportBodyLowLatency {`

WHY THE COST WAS SO FAR ABOVE THE DEFECT. The refusal is a DESYNCHRONISE, and
a desync abandons every byte behind it. One unreadable Declare therefore cost
the capture its entire remaining stream, including the KeepAlives and the
Close that this build decodes perfectly well. The distinction the repair turns
on is one the refused predicate's own doc already states: strictness is the
right test for a SCAN over bytes whose framing is unknown, and the wrong one
at a boundary the reader is already synchronised to. This gate is only ever
asked just past a length prefix it has already read.

DECIDED, and stated as a limit rather than left implied: this round does NOT
decode those messages. A bare `NetworkMessage` still has no arm in
`InboundFrame`, so the eight that now appear are located and named BY MID and
their bodies are not read. That is a model, not a patch -- `InboundFrame::` is
matched at 245 sites across five crates -- and it is registered rather than
smuggled in behind a one-line gate change.
verification_bullets: END TO END ON THE REPORTER'S OWN CAPTURE, through the door their tool calls
(`wz_dissect_pcap_fields_limited`, driven by dlopening the built cdylib):
negotiated-lowlatency.pcap   4 messages  ->  15
session.pcap (the control)  99 messages  ->  99
15 is every frame on the wire, counted independently by parsing the pcap and
walking each direction's TCP stream by hand. The 15 are Init x2, Open x2,
Unknown x8, KeepAlive x2, Close x1 -- and the KeepAlives and the Close are the
part that matters, because they were already decodable and the desync was
eating them.

MEASUREMENTS THAT RULED CANDIDATES OUT, recorded because each was a wrong
answer this round believed for a while:
* TCP segment size is NOT the cause -- a copy of the capture with every large
segment split into 512-byte ones reads the same 4 messages.
* The capture has no truncation (snaplen 262144, 0 truncated) and no TCP
sequence gap in either direction.
* The negotiated `batch_size` (256, against 4120-byte frames) is NOT the
cause: `exceeds_batch` flags and does not drop, which its own test name
says.
* The prefix WIDTH is not the cause. This round first concluded it was, from
walking the stream with a 2-byte prefix and seeing garbage, and never
checked what this reader actually chose. R2789's per-direction reframing was
correct and complete; the bisect test above is what settled it.

Round 2804.decision_summary:
Give `storage-backend-filesystem` its foreign witness: upstream's own
filesystem backend reads what wz wrote into a directory, and wz reads what

WHY A WITNESS WAS NEEDED AT ALL. R2801 made the directory's metadata upstream's
own `.zenoh_datainfo` RocksDB rows, byte for byte, and every test of that format
compared wz with bytes DERIVED from upstream's source. A derivation wrong the
same way in the encoder and the decoder passes all of those. Only upstream's
code can say whether upstream agrees.

THE ORACLE, and why it is a library caller. `oracles/fs-backend` links
`zenoh-backend-filesystem` 1.10.1 (git tag, the pin the reference clone sits
on) in the oracle workspace, whose `[patch.crates-io]` redirects the backend's
crates.io zenoh names onto the pinned tag so one zenoh is compiled. It starts
upstream's volume through its own `Plugin::start` (root from
`ZENOH_BACKEND_FS_ROOT`), configures the storage through upstream's own
`PluginConfig` parser, and calls its `Storage` impl. zenohd plus the plugin
was the other route; a `dlopen`ed backend must match the router's zenoh
version AND feature set, and the claim is about the directory, which the
`Storage` impl writes and reads whatever loads it.

FIVE LEGS, compared as one line over every field and against the line the
written values predict, so two implementations agreeing on a wrong answer
cannot pass: upstream writes and wz reads (including `@root`); wz writes and
upstream reads; a prefix conflict laid down by one side and moved aside, row
and all, by the other, both ways; a file nobody put, read the same way by both;
and a delete by wz that upstream sees, row included -- proven by putting an
operator's file back at the deleted key and requiring upstream to stamp it as
a file with no row. All five passed on their first run. Layer E16 runs them in
the `interop` job, the one that caches `oracles/target`.

THE GATE THIS EXPOSED. Layer E sweeps the crate's ignored tests minus name
tokens and builds no oracle; `layer_e_oracle_scope_gate.py` exists to refuse a
selected test that reaches an unprovisioned binary, and its helper list named

so these legs would have been adopted by a lane that cannot run them; E8t's
`future-stamp` legs had stayed out only because their names carry `wz_router`.
The helper joined the list, and the legs carry the `fs_shared_dir` token.

Grade `storage-backend-filesystem` COMPLETE, after closing the three
differences a re-reading of both backends found once the foreign witness
was green.

WHAT THE VOLUME REPORTS. Upstream's storage manager answers
`status/plugins/storage_manager/volumes/<id>` with the volume instance's own
status, and its fs volume answers with the root and version its plugin `start`
records. wz answered every volume with its capability, on R311y828's premise
that a wz volume has no configuration to echo -- refuted for this volume by
R2802, which derives its root exactly as upstream's does. The premise is
re-scoped rather than discarded: `Volume::admin_status(version)` defaults to
the capability body and the filesystem volume overrides it with
`{"root": ..., "version": ...}`, root canonical, keys in serde's map order. The
memory volume keeps its body, pinned beside the fs one in the same test.

THE DIRECTORY SYNC OFF UNIX. `fsync_dir` opened the directory as a file; windows
refuses that without a flag `std` does not set, so every write there would have
failed at its first directory sync. Off unix it is a no-op now -- never weaker
than upstream, which syncs nothing anywhere. Found by reading after R2802 made
the backend buildable off unix; no lane here builds it there.

A DEFECT R2802 INTRODUCED. Typing `volume_cfg` made the storage admin body write
each value's JSON5 SOURCE spelling, so a config's `0x10` or `+1` made the whole
body unparseable by a JSON reader, where upstream renders through `serde_json`.

string rather than rounded), and the admin body uses it. It was the one site:
the manager's other two renderings hand text to a backend or a loaded volume.

THE GRADE. Every upstream behavior of the backend at 1.10.1 -- layout, sidecar,
no-row fallbacks, the five properties and every refusal, the root, the kept
config, read-only, closure, capability and now status -- is witnessed by a test

claim by upstream's own backend in both directions. The divergences left are all
safer or stronger (durable writes, payload before row, delete-every-holder, the
refused keys and links) or refusal texts that name a different reason for the
same refusal; each is stated in the reason where it lives.

Round 2805.decision_summary:
Recover the two interrupted sessions and move the CI RocksDB build outside Cargo feature units. The previous push stopped at a crates.io DNS failure in the feature diagnostic, not at a Rust diagnostic. Its 105 probes pass on retry.

The abandoned engine draft could not build: Cargo rejects feature selection on a dependency outside the workspace. Its two-archive approach also treated the wz snappy-only build and the upstream oracle full-codec build as the same feature set. The replacement builds the checksum-pinned librocksdb-sys source with its bundled RocksDB CMake recipe as a portable shared library. All five codecs are available to the two Rust callers, with their dependencies linked by the native library. Workspace and oracle lock pins must agree before an engine is selected.

Eight native Linux CI jobs opt in through one composite action. The key includes the source checksum, recipe, host and C++ compiler. Cache restores check identity and library digest, then compile and run a version and five-codec flush/reopen probe. A missing or corrupt engine is rebuilt in a staging directory. Saving immediately after provisioning keeps a later test failure or timeout from discarding the engine.

The apt census now follows local composite actions and Python build drivers, so the native CMake dependency is observed rather than exempted. Ordinary local builds, release packaging and cross-platform jobs retain the crate build. This is CI provisioning, not a change to the filesystem format or its public API. Hosted job-budget improvement remains to be measured on the deployed workflow.

Round 2808.decision_summary: Close open-debt item 815 by removing spinlock-backed 64-bit atomics from the SysTick clock. The current HEAD reproduces the hosted reassembly hang: QEMU stopped in SysTick at PC 0x4e6 while the stacked thread PC 0x675c was inside OpenAck construction. Grade `query-get` COMPLETE: a refused keyed reply now returns its Err to

WHICH ATOM. At 792ae7be REMAINING was 18. R2811 (the previous round of this
run) re-measured `routing-peer` and left it PARTIAL on residuals that are
each more than a round: a namespace layer, a non-tcp mesh dial whose address
is the currency of the whole re-dial machinery, and unmeasured peer
interests. `query-get` was re-measured next, residual by residual, and it was
the one whose remaining clauses were all inside this repository: (a) the
reply refusal did not reach the caller, (b) no foreign binary had read the
refusal, (c) a third `_anyke` parse in `wz-capi-c`. All ten sibling query
atoms were already COMPLETE.

THE BASE. The refusal was COUNTED on the responder because the `ReplyOut`
seam returned `()`. Nothing read the count, and the handler that made the
mistake could not. Upstream's replier gets the `bail!` back
(`zenoh/src/api/queryable.rs` @ `which does not intersect with query`), so
the seam itself was the defect: every keyed arm now returns
`Result<(), ReplyError>`. The bound-keyexpr arms and `reply_err` stay `()`,
since they stage under the query's own keyexpr or none and have nothing to
refuse. Each production caller takes upstream's handling for the same site.

THE WITNESS. A stock querier drops an out-of-query reply itself, so "it
never printed" cannot tell a wz refusal from a zenoh drop. zenoh LOGS its
drop (`zenoh/src/api/session.rs` @ `which didn't match query`), so a default
get must leave that warning absent, and a `?_anyke` get must see both keys.

(c) WAS STALE. R2306 had already routed `wz-capi-c`'s reader through
`ReplyKeyExpr::from_parameters`; the reason still called it open.

WHAT NO FOREIGN BINARY CAN DECIDE: wz's requester-side refusal. A conforming
responder refuses an out-of-query reply before it is sent, so against stock
zenoh or pico that gate has no input. Recorded in the reason as a limit of
observation, not a residual.

Round 2814.decision_summary:
Build the base of ext-pubsub-advanced-subscriber's API residual: a
miss-listener registry, and a Miss whose source is one EntityGlobalId.

WHICH ATOM. At c7b70d42 REMAINING was 17. Hosted run 35850062256 was red
on C0 and Layer E; R2813 had already paid it (test_discipline_gate --check
rc 0 here), so no CI round was owed. Candidates were measured by reading
each residual against code: routing-peer carries an owner fork (the
linkstate default) and an unmeasured interest plane; runtime-zero-copy has
no live residual to build (R2757); the platform and qos atoms wait on CI
hosts or an async-TX decision. ext-pubsub-advanced-subscriber's residuals
are all wz-side and derivable from zenoh-ext at the pin, and R2619 had
already closed the same handle surface on the advanced publisher.

THE BASE. Upstream declares a subscriber with no miss callback and adds
listeners afterwards, any number, each retractable:
`zenoh-ext/src/advanced_subscriber.rs` @ `miss_handlers: HashMap<usize, Callback<Miss>>,`
wz took exactly one on_miss closure at declare. That one
fact generated two defects outside this module: both C ABIs adapted to it
with a single slot a listener "installed into", so a second listener
replaced the first and retracting the first silenced the second; and the
zenoh-pico ABI's background form delegated to the owned form with a null
handle, which the owned form refuses after consuming the closure, so every
background miss listener was dropped and the call returned Z_ERR_NULL.

WHAT WAS BUILT. MissHandlers inside State; AdvancedSubscriber::
sample_miss_listener (callback) and sample_miss_listener_with_channel
(the default FIFO form); SampleMissListener with undeclare, background and
drop-retracts, holding the state weakly. Miss is { source: EntityGlobalId,
nb } behind accessors, as upstream's. EntityGlobalId is a new
wz-session-core value type (padded zid + len + eid, equality and hash on
the prefix only); SourceInfo::source_id returns it, and route_sample now
treats an out-of-range zid as no source, which is SourceInfo's own
documented contract. In wz-capi-core, ListenerSet<C> is the C-level fan-in:
each face's wz subscriber reports into it, each C listener owns one entry,
and calls and drops happen outside its lock.

ONE ADDITION UPSTREAM DOES NOT HAVE. declare_with_options_and_miss_listener
seeds one listener before the startup history GET is issued. The C ABIs
re-declare one logical subscriber per face and the demo grades its
ADVANCED MISS line; for both, a listener declared after declare could miss
holes that a GET completing inside the call reports.

compiled under it; hot reload and router-config-mutate require it;

avoids that by giving each link a stats handle holding its own counters. wz
now does the same with a LinkSlot: a link opens once and is recorded on by
index, its three link-scoped families keyed by Copy labels only. The
transport-level bucket (upstream's None link) holds payload histograms and the
cells a closed link folds into. The seven golden scenarios stayed green
across the refactor, which is what they are for.

WHY THE LINK GAUGE IS DERIVED. A session will keep its own partition and hand
it to the node registry (set_transport_metrics), so no open or close event
passes through the registry. Upstream's gauge is +1 on open, -1 on close and
never drops its series: that is the count of open links plus a zero series
for every protocol seen, which the partition already holds.

THE KIND. NetworkStatsClass carried the JSON schema's axis, which has no kind
for a control message and folds reply-err onto reply. It now carries the
registry's nine-way MessageLabel as a constructor parameter, so each typed
sender must say what it sends. Every Request is a query, as upstream labels
it. An undecoded body (a build without the codec) is left unlabelled rather
than guessed: the MID constants that would name it are gated on that codec.

First slice of giving an MCU upstream's runtime connection control: the

Round 2825.decision_summary:
Record into the stats registry from the session seams, and make the sizes
and counts it records upstream's.

RECORDING. SessionCore keeps its own TransportMetrics under a per-session
lock; each LinkState holds its slot, opened from the driver's own locator
pair at construction (a driver that names no endpoints gets no slot rather
than invented labels). Three seams, placed where upstream places them:
- a SENT wire write counts bytes and one transport message on its link;
- dispatch_network_message observes the payload at entry (upstream observes
  in the dispatcher, before any link), counts the network message on the
  link its conduit is routed to, and a message no link can take is a
  `no-link` dropped payload, upstream's tx_observe_no_link;
- the RX walk observes and counts each decoded network message on the
  receiving link under the message's OWN band (read off its ext_qos, a
  push reader added beside the others).
A link joining a multilink aggregate is re-opened in the primary's
partition and leaving closes it there, since a slot indexes one partition.

(1) Item 820: payload size left out the attachment, counted a Del as 0 and
a Query as its parameters. Upstream's payload_size() is payload +
attachment, a Del's attachment, a Query's body value without its encoding

capability to SEND one; they moved into the ungated body-extension table,
and the value split into one encoding::split_value_body.
(2) RX t_msgs counted reads; upstream counts per decoded message inside
its batch walk, and zenoh batches by default. It now counts in
dispatch_unit, one per message decoded off the unit.

MEASURED FIRST. wz-session-lwip's session drive decodes every inbound frame
and hands the batch to its caller's `on_event`, and nothing in production

Third ZA-2898 slice: an MCU node hosts upstream's connect/endpoints write.

BUILT: `wz-session-lwip::admin_host`. `host_connect_writes` registers, on the
node's application-layer observer (R2827's seam), a subscriber for the node's
own config space `@/<zid>/<whatami>/config/**`, the key upstream's admin space
subscribes to. Each sample is decided by R2824's `admin_connect` and applied
to a `ConnectControl`: a PUT replaces the endpoint list, a DEL removes it, and
anything refused (denied, malformed, too many, too long) changes nothing.

WHY THE CONTROL IS A `&'static`: the observer's subscriber registry is the
AP's too and takes `Send` callbacks, while the MCU session bundle is `Rc`
because `alloc::sync::Arc` does not exist on ARMv6-M. A node's connection
control lives as long as the firmware, so it is a `critical_section::Mutex`
behind a `'static`, which is `Send + Sync` on every target without an `Arc`.
It carries a generation that moves on every applied write, for the dial
layer (the next slice) to know when to act, and the last verdict, because
upstream only logs a refused write.

The feature needs both sample kinds, so `adminspace-write` on this crate pulls
`pubsub-put` and `pubsub-delete`.

take full paths, and C1cn's wz-session-lwip leg names `adminspace-write` and
`pubsub-put`. The second also covers R2827's app-layer test, which needs

Round 2830.decision_summary:
Fifth ZA-2898 slice, the first half of "dial and re-dial per endpoint":
the MCU node now keeps a session with every endpoint its connection
control names, and re-dials the ones that drop, on upstream's own
`connect.retry` schedule.

BUILT: `connect_manager::ConnectManager`, ticked by the firmware's main
loop. On a new control generation it reconciles (an endpoint no longer
named is hung up, a new one is dialled at once); a session that ends is
scheduled for its re-dial; whatever is due is dialled. The dialling is
behind a `Dialer` trait, so the bookkeeping is decided and tested with no
network; the lwIP dialer is the next slice.

THE SCHEDULE IS THE AP'S, NOT A SECOND TRANSCRIPTION: `retry_period`
(upstream's 1000 / 4000 / x2 period) moved from wz-runtime-tokio into
wz-session-core, and wz-runtime-tokio re-exports it. One transcription,
two runtimes. A session that ends BEFORE establishing continues the same
outage's period; one that ends AFTER establishing starts a fresh period,
as upstream builds one per outage.

A REFUSED DIAL IS NOT RETRIED: an endpoint this build cannot dial at all
(no link for its scheme, an address it cannot parse) waits for the list
to be written again, the only event that can change the answer. Retrying
it would be the hot loop the schedule exists to prevent.

BUILT: `lwip_dialer::LwipUdpDialer`, the lwIP `Dialer` for R2830's
connection manager. A dial binds a session socket on an ephemeral port
(lwIP picks it), points an `LwipUdpDriver` at the endpoint, and spawns an
INITIATOR session with `spawn_session`, the same call a deploy writes for
its one compiled-in peer. What this build cannot dial is refused, not
retried: another scheme, or upstream's `?metadata` / `#config` parts, as
Unsupported (the link honours neither, and dialling anyway would drop what
the writer asked for); a host name as BadAddress (no resolver). A node
that cannot afford a socket answers the new `DialFailed::Exhausted`,
which waits its period as an unanswered dial would.

A DEFECT THE DIALER FOUND, FIXED HERE: the MCU pump activated an
initiator with `OutboundStart` alone. The AP's `initiator_open` raises
`OutboundStart` then `LinkOpened`; the second is what enters SentInitSyn
and sends the InitSyn. So every MCU initiator sat in LinkOpening, silent
on the wire. Nothing had driven one before: the MCU deploys are
acceptors. `SessionRole::activation` now returns both events.

A FEATURE GAP THE SAME TEST FOUND: InitSyn / OpenSyn are emitted only
under wz-session-core `session-unicast-open` with the Init and Open body
codecs, and nothing in wz-session-lwip enabled them. A node that accepts
an endpoint list must be able to dial it, so `adminspace-write` now pulls
the initiator half. The acceptor half is a dev feature, for the test.

THE WITNESS IS A REAL HANDSHAKE: the test dials an acceptor on the same
lwIP loopback and both ends reach Established. Its first runs failed three
ways, each a finding above or the acceptor's fail-closed cookie (an
acceptor with no entropy source mints no cookie, R2763), and the passing
run is the one after all three were paid.

Round 2835.decision_summary:
First part of ZA-2898's last slice (a stock zenoh host writing the list
and reading the status of a wz MCU under QEMU). Every lwIP stack in this
tree ran over the loopback netif alone, so an MCU node had no way to
reach anything outside its own process. This round builds that way out:
an Ethernet netif whose MAC is a Rust driver.

WHY ETHERNET, AND NOT A SERIAL BRIDGE: QEMU's mps2 boards carry a
LAN9118 Ethernet controller (base 0x40200000 on an385/an386/an511,
0xa0000000 on an500, per QEMU 8.2.2 `hw/arm/mps2.c`), and QEMU's user
networking gives a guest a routed host without privileges. An Ethernet
netif is also what a board deploy uses, so the lane will exercise the
path a real node takes rather than a test-only one. The lwIP ports in
this tree already enable ARP and Ethernet.

THE SPLIT, AND WHY IT IS C WHERE IT IS: lwIP's own `ethernetif` template
is an init callback filling netif fields (flags, hwaddr, `output` =
`etharp_output`, `linkoutput`) and an input path handing a pbuf to
`netif->input`. Those are struct fields and macro-sized constants, and
the bindgen `netif` is opaque in some ports, which is the reason R2390's
carrier seam is C too. So `shim.c` gains `wz_ethif_add` and
`wz_ethif_input`, and Rust keeps only the MAC behind `EthernetMac`
(send one whole frame; hand whole frames in). Receive is polled from the
firmware's loop. Ports without ARP/Ethernet compile the two entry points
as refusals, so the bound symbol set does not depend on the port.

THE WITNESS IS THE CABLE: the test plays the far host at the frame
level. A send leaves as an ARP request for the far address and nothing
else; after the test's ARP reply, the queued datagram leaves as an
Ethernet/IPv4/UDP frame to the MAC the reply named; a UDP frame the test
sends in reaches the bound socket. A first version put two interfaces in
the one lwIP stack and failed: the later-added interface owns the route
to its own address and lwIP loops it back without the cable. That shape
cannot test a cable, so the far host became the test.

Round 2836.decision_summary:
Second part of ZA-2898's last slice: the Ethernet MAC a wz MCU node uses
under QEMU, an SMSC LAN9118, behind R2835's `EthernetMac`.

WHERE THE BEHAVIOUR CAME FROM: QEMU 8.2.2's model of the part, the one
the lanes run against, read directly rather than recalled: the register
offsets, `BYTE_TEST` reading 0x87654321, soft reset through `HW_CFG`,
MAC control registers reached through `MAC_CSR_CMD` / `MAC_CSR_DATA`
(`MAC_CR` with TXEN and RXEN; the station address in `ADDRL` / `ADDRH`),
transmit as command A (FIRST, LAST, buffer size) and command B (tag,
packet length) followed by little-endian data words, receive as a status
word whose length counts the 4-byte FCS followed by that many bytes in
whole words. The model clears the busy bits at once and ignores TX_ON;
the driver still polls and still sets it, as the part requires.

WHAT IS TESTED WITHOUT A BOARD: the packing is split into `tx_words` and
`rx_unpack`, which touch no register. The tests transcribe the model's
own transmit reassembly and receive packing and hold the driver to them
at every length residue modulo 4, the 42-byte ARP minimum and a full
1514-byte frame. A frame the driver cannot keep (too long, in error) is
still drained word for word, so the next frame's words are never read as
its tail. The MMIO path itself is exercised only on the part or in QEMU,
which is the lane's job.

Round 2837.decision_summary:
Third part of ZA-2898's last slice: the MCU node as ONE thing a firmware
ticks. `admin_node::AdminNode` wires the earlier rounds' pieces to one
application-layer observer (the config-write subscriber, the admin GET
queryable, the connection manager and its lwIP dialer) and adds the half
none of them had: a session a host can reach the node on at all.

WHAT IT DOES: the node LISTENS on a UDP port with an acceptor session; a
host that connects there can write `connect/endpoints` and GET the
status. When that session ends, the node listens again on the next tick.
Every session, accepted or dialled, dispatches to the same observer, so a
write or a GET is answered the same way on any of them. Each tick reports
every ESTABLISHED session, accepted and dialled, as the GET's `sessions`,
which is how upstream lists transports; `admin_session_of` is the one
rendering both use.

A FEATURE GAP THE COMPOSITION EXPOSED, PAID HERE: R2831 put the acceptor
half of the handshake (`session-unicast-accept`) in a DEV feature, for the
dialer's test peer. With a listener in the library, that would have been
a node whose listener accepts nothing in any real build while its tests
pass. `adminspace-write` now pulls it, beside the initiator half, and the
dev feature is gone; the adminspace-write leg still passes 9 without it.

THE WITNESS: end to end over lwIP loopback, a write arriving on the
node's observer makes it dial a peer; the peer completes the handshake;
the node then reports that peer's zid. Its control is the same node
before the write: listening, reporting nothing, dialling nothing.

LINK ENDS: an MCU session's `links` read `{"src":"","dst":""}`, because
the MCU UDP driver never implemented `link_endpoints`. It now does, in
upstream's rendering, `udp/<ip>:<port>` each. A UDP pcb bound to any
address has no source of its own, so the source is what lwIP routes the
peer through: `wz_lwip_route_src` (`ip4_route` plus the netif's address,
C macros, so in `shim.c` beside the carrier and Ethernet seams) with the
pcb's bound port (`wz_lwip_udp_local_port`). The pair is written ONCE,
when the peer is first known: at construction for an initiator, at the
first datagram for an acceptor. Once written it names the link; a later
datagram from elsewhere does not rename it.

ENDPOINT GROUPS: upstream's `connect/endpoints` elements are a string or
a `{ strategy, locators }` object (its `EndPoints` is untagged). The MCU
surface refused the object. It now reads it as upstream's visitor does:
`commons/zenoh-protocol/src/core/endpoint.rs` @ `struct LocatorsHelper {`
Both members required and each at most once, `allOf` / `oneOf`, any other member
skipped (the helper struct does not deny unknown fields). The list is
kept flat, each entry carrying its group, so the no-alloc storage stays
one fixed array; an empty group is one entry with no endpoint so it
reads back. The config read-back renders groups exactly as upstream
serializes `Locators`. Dialling: a group of ONE locator is dialled like
a bare endpoint. A group of several means one transport over several
links (`AllOf`, the only strategy upstream's runtime implements); an MCU
session holds one link, so each of its locators is refused by name,
`DialRefused::MultiLinkGroup`, rather than dialled as separate sessions
to what is one peer.

Round 2844.decision_summary:
A node keeps ONE stats registry across every transport it holds, recorded
where its sessions are driven, and every admin host serves it.

THE BASE. Upstream's transport manager registers a unicast transport's
stats when it is established (`io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/manager.rs` @
`let stats = self.stats.unicast_transport_stats(`) and drops them when it
closes. A wz mesh node's transport manager is the face loop: every face of a
peer or a router enters the held set at one site and leaves it at one of
two. `node_stats::NodeStats` is recorded from exactly those sites through a
new `FaceSources.stats` field, so no host re-learns the face lifecycle. The
storage host drives its own sessions, one client at a time in sequence, and
records each as a transport too; a registry built from the current session
alone would have dropped every earlier session's counts. The labels come
from one function, `SessionLinkActions::open_stats_transport`, which the
one-session registry now uses as well. A closed transport is marked
disconnected and retired after the collection delay, by the collection that
crosses it, which is upstream's order (`commons/zenoh-stats/src/family.rs`
@ `if garbage_collection {`). `NodeStats::for_node` answers None in a build
without `transport-stats`, so a host serves build info alone, the pin's
not-stats arm, without knowing the feature.

A DEFECT FOUND ON THE WAY, FIXED AT ITS BASE. Every forwarder-hosted admin
leg answered with no selector parameters: the forwarder's `LocalQueryView`
returned None, on a Phase-2a premise that the admin handler read only the
key. It had read `descriptors` since R2494 and the four partitions since
R2843, so on every peer and router those were ignored. And a Session-hosted
leg saw none either unless `query-selector-parameters` was built in. Now
`adminspace-metrics` implies that projection, and both paths read one
function, `query::query_parameters` (the deferred self-query keeps its
parameters too).

A SECOND ONE, in the witness's own tool: `wz-e2e-admin-probe` documented
`--get <SELECTOR>` and sent the whole string as a key expression, so
`metrics?per_link=false` matched nothing and read as a host that answered
nothing. It now splits at `?` and carries the parameters on the Query.

WHY THE WITNESS IS NOT PICO. The registry document of a one-transport node
measured 5142 bytes; pico's default reassembly bound is 4096 and its z_get
sends no parameters. Upstream would gzip the body; wz does not, by the
owner's decision on item 677. That decision now has a measured consequence
worth knowing; it is recorded here, not re-opened.

Round 2846.decision_summary:
ZA-2929, from the analyzer: when an MCU refuses a `connect/endpoints`
write, or refuses to dial an endpoint, the reason never reached the host.
The write verdict (`ConnectControl::last_outcome`) and each endpoint's
state (`SlotState::Refused(DialRefused)`) were device-side APIs only, and
the admin GET carried neither, so a host could only watch the session
list not change and could not tell "refused" from "not dialled yet" from
"unreachable". The analyzer's design requires a refusal to carry the
device's own words, and asked for it to stay readable with writes off.

WHERE IT LIVES: a new admin key, `@/<zid>/<whatami>/status/connect`.
Upstream refuses such a write by logging it and nothing else, so there
is no upstream key to put the answer in; this is a wz extension, and it
is kept OUT of the legs that mirror upstream (`local_data`, `config`) so
a stock host reads those exactly as before. It sits under `status/`,
beside upstream's `status/plugins`. The root GET does not carry it; a
`**` GET does, as it reaches every admin key.

WHAT IT SAYS: `{"permissions":{"write":…},"last_write":…,"endpoints":
[…]}`. `last_write` is `null` before the first write, else the verdict
by its own name (`denied`, `replace`, `too_many`, …), and a malformed
value adds where the parse stopped and what it expected. Each endpoint
is `live` (with `established`), `waiting` (with `retry_in_ms`), or
`refused` (with `reason`: `unsupported`, `bad_address`,
`multi_link_group`).

GATED BY THE READ PERMIT ALONE, as every admin leg is, so a node whose
write permit is off still answers here, with `"write":false` and the
`denied` verdict: the host can tell "writes are off" from "my write was
lost".

THE WITNESS, AGAINST A STOCK ZENOHD: Layer Qa gains Qa.5 (after the
write, the verdict is `replace` and B is `live`, `established`) and Qa.6
(a two-locator group is written; both locators read `refused`,
`multi_link_group`). Local runs of the lane: one green at Qa.1-Qa.6; one
earlier run at a host load over 25 lost both sessions before Qa.6's
write (lease expiry under a starved QEMU) and the node was not reached
again within its 30 s. That second part is its own question, carried.

(1) status/connect's last_write now carries `seq`, the number of writes the node has received counting the one it reports, so a host that reads seq before it writes (null reads as 0) owns any verdict whose seq is higher; verdict and seq are read under one lock so they always describe the same write. On the MCU node's fixed 4 KB heap that ran the heap dry within seconds, the node stopped sending, and every accepted session died about 15 s after it opened, which is why Qa.6 lost its B session when it ran late. The host port never showed it because it allocates from libc malloc, so no host test can discriminate this leak; the discriminating witness is the QEMU node. Round 2853.decision_summary:
Pay the Layer Qa red of run 36002723608: `zenohd not at
target/zenohd/zenohd` on `cross-mcu`.

RE-MEASURED, NOT INHERITED. R2842 recorded this red paid by ordering
`cross-mcu` after `interop`, and that commit is in the red run's tree. So
the ordering held and the diagnosis did not. The interop job saved the
zenohd cache entry at 15:03:56; `cross-mcu`, queued, restored at 20:26 and
found neither the key nor the prefix. The repository's cache list now
holds 23 entries, 13.6 GB, and no zenohd entry at all: evicted in between,
with every per-job rust cache re-saving about 1 GB per run.

THE BASE. A cache is a best-effort store shared by all runs; nothing
promises an entry survives until a later job of the same run reads it.
The carrier for a file between two jobs of one run is a run artifact,
which belongs to that run and is not evicted by other runs' saves. So
interop now tars its asserted `target/zenohd` (upload drops the exec bit
Layer Qa tests) into the runner's temp directory and publishes it right
after its pin assert, so a later red in its own lanes still leaves the
oracle; `cross-mcu` downloads and unpacks it before the pin gate reads it.
When interop never reached the publish step the download fails and Layer
Qa is not reached, which is the truth rather than another run's entry.
Layers G and Q run before that step and are unaffected.

NOT PROVEN HERE. Only a hosted run can prove it: actionlint is clean on
the workflow and the lane script parses, and the next run carrying this
commit is the witness.

Round 2858.decision_summary:
Build adminspace-core's `region` residual. The atom stays PARTIAL on
three residuals. REMAINING 14 -> 14.

The pin writes a `region` per unicast session
(`zenoh/src/net/runtime/adminspace.rs` @ `let transport_unicast_to_region = move |transport: &TransportUnicast| -> Option<Region> {`),
from this node's mode, the peer's, and the bound the peer announced on
its Open (`commons/zenoh-protocol/src/transport/open.rs`
@ `pub type RemoteBound = zextz64!(0x7, false);`). wz read no such
extension and wrote no such field.

Upstream sends the bound only when its gateway preset is custom, and
under the default Auto preset the region is `compute_auto_region`'s
table. `gateway/south` is not a key wz honours, so a wz node is always
on Auto: its transient region is None and only the first three arms of
`compute_region_of` are reachable. `extbound` mirrors those arms and the
auto table; `unknown` is each `bail!`.

The bound is read off both Opens and admitted before the Open's other
state. A present value that is neither bound after upstream's `as u8`
truncation refuses the handshake with GENERIC, as upstream's two receive
arms do. Every admin host fills the field from one method on the session
actions, so no host can compute it differently.

Note: id `0x7` is PATCH on the Init carrier and REMOTE-BOUND on the Open
carrier. The reader is fed an Open's chain only.

The witness was built (upstream z_pub_shm -> tap -> wz, an inline leg
that must show the payload on the wire and an SHM leg that must deliver

the codec, not the test: upstream writes an SHM Put's payload in its

probe with a header-bit predicate generates the needed repeat and
optional fields, and the chain predicate is refused at the parser.
Per owner instruction SCE is read-only here: the gap is reported in
SCE's claudedocs and filed as debt 823. The witness is held on the
local branch hold/shm-payload-witness rather than committed as a
claim it cannot yet make. This round lands 3c849c6f (every Session
installs the POSIX resolver; the shm zenohd build also installs

carry_forward_bullets: Next is item 751 step 3e: the register-in-owner + propagate(other_info) dispatch. The pin's shape was read this round (`zenoh/src/net/routing/dispatcher/pubsub.rs` @ `hats[dst].propagate_subscriber(ctx.reborrow(), res.clone(), other_info);`). Declaring registers the declaration in `hats[face.region]`, then for EVERY region `dst` computes `other_info` as the fold of `remote_subscribers_of` over the hats other than `dst`, and calls `hats[dst].propagate_subscriber`. Undeclaring unregisters from the owner and collects the hats that still hold the resource: if none remain, every hat unpropagates; if exactly one remains, that `last_owner` calls `unpropagate_last_non_owned_subscriber`.

In wz, the per-hat `other_info` fold is what `derived_cross_tier_*` and the `advertise_client_cross_tier_*` / `withdraw_native_cross_tier_*` pairs compute today, hand-split by mesh versus client. Step 3e is the point where the `if is_leaf(tier)` split at the declare dispatch collapses into one owner call plus the propagate loop.

The 3e design derived from the code this round: `self_advertises_sub_into(target, K)` is ALREADY the pin's `other_info` for a mesh target, i.e. "some hat other than `target` holds K" (broker hats, the opposite mesh, the group, the host). What is hand-written is the flip-edge detection: four advertise/withdraw pairs per plane (client, group, native, and the host path), each re-deriving "was this the first/last contributor" from its own kind. One dispatch replaces them: evaluate the predicate for every mesh target BEFORE the owner-hat mutation, mutate, evaluate AFTER, then flood a declare where false->true and an undeclare where true->false. That is derive-not-store kept intact (no advertised bit is stored), and it is the same loop for subs, qabls (with the merged-info change as the edge) and tokens.

Round 2875.decision_summary:
R2875 takes open-debt item 751 step 3e for the queryable plane, the half R2874's carry left: the register-in-owner + propagate dispatch where the edge is a VALUE, not a presence flip.

The pin's queryable propagate stores, per hat, the info it last propagated, and re-propagates only when the new fold of the other hats differs (`zenoh/src/net/routing/hat/router/queries.rs` @ `.is_none_or(|info| info != &other_info)`); its dispatcher runs that for every region after registering in the owner (`zenoh/src/net/routing/dispatcher/queries.rs` @ `tables.hats[dst].propagate_queryable(ctx.reborrow(), res.clone(), other_info);`). wz re-flooded both meshes on every register and re-declared the fold on every withdrawal whatever it was. The downstream value-diff gate absorbed those, but they were wire traffic the pin never sends.

The presence planes' derive (R2874: "held outside T, not counting one contribution") does not carry over. A queryable register can REPLACE a value, and a face-down or Oam-detach purge removes several sources' values at once, so the before-state is not recoverable from the after-state and one holder. The before-state is therefore READ: `snapshot_qabl` records the merged info outside each mesh region before the mutation, and `repropagate_qabl` diffs it after, flooding a `DeclareQueryable` with the new fold where it changed and an `UndeclareQueryable` where it emptied. Nothing is stored between changes: the snapshot is the value the previous change propagated, by induction over the same rule.

To read the keyexpr before a mesh table changes, the resolve half of `ingest_interest` / `withdraw_interest` was split out (`resolve_sourced` -> `Sourced`), with `commit_register` / `commit_withdraw` as the mutating half; the sub and token planes compose the same halves and are unchanged in behaviour. Every qabl path routes through the snapshot: mesh ingest and withdraw, the purge (which reads the departing peers' keys before removing them), client ingest and withdraw, deregister, and host registration.

`derived_cross_tier_qabl_info` is now a fold over `Holder`s outside the target (`qabl_contribution`), and `derived_cross_tier_qabls_into` a filter of it over `qabl_keys`, the same construction the presence planes got. The host contributor was measured first and is already exact per keyexpr here, so the sub plane's intersection defect does not recur. Five per-kind qabl functions and `opposite_mesh`, now without a caller, are removed: the mesh targets are read off the region map.

The pin propagates every plane by the same rule: a hat compares the other hats' fold against what it last propagated. ` / `repropagate

R2878 takes open-debt item 751 step 4, the one R2876's carry named: the linkstate gateway bit. It is the input step 5's inter-region filter reads, and the only step of the nine that changes what wz puts on the wire.

The pin carries it as a flag with no field: bit 4 of the link-state options word (`zenoh/src/net/protocol/linkstate.rs` @ `pub const GWY: u64 = 1 << 4;`), written when the node is a gateway and read back into `is_gateway` (`zenoh/src/net/codec/linkstate.rs` @ `let is_gateway = imsg::has_option(options, linkstate::GWY);`). wz's codec already carried the options byte raw, so a zenohd gateway's bit arrived and was dropped on the floor by the graph; nothing in wz could emit it.

Where each piece lives, read from the pin rather than chosen:
- A net's self node is a gateway exactly when the net serves a south region, fixed at construction at sn 1 (`zenoh/src/net/protocol/network.rs` @ `is_gateway: bound.is_south(),`). wz gains `LinkstateNetwork::new_in_region`; `new` stays the north-bound case, as the pin's `Bound::default()` is `North`. A setter was written first and dropped: the pin never changes the bit after construction, and a setter had to invent an sn bump the pin does not have.
- The router seeds each mesh hat's net from that hat's region (`zenoh/src/net/routing/hat/router/mod.rs` @ `self.region().bound(),`), so a wz router advertises G into its south peer region and not into the router mesh. That is the wire change: zenohd peers now see a wz router as their region's gateway, as they see a zenohd router.
- Every entry of a gateway node carries G, relayed ones and every form included, since the pin reads the node, not the entry's details (`zenoh/src/net/protocol/network.rs` @ `is_gateway: self.graph[idx].is_gateway,`).
- The linkstate ingest restates the bit on every newer state, so a cleared bit clears it (`zenoh/src/net/protocol/network.rs` @ `node.is_gateway = ls.is_gateway;`). The gossip ingest takes it on insert only and leaves it on update, which is what the pin's `process_singlehop_gossip_linkstate` does; mirrored, not chosen. A placeholder or a link-introduced neighbour carries no bit until its own state does, as in the pin's `Network::add_link`.
- `gateways` and `gateways_of` read the bit as the pin's router and peer hats do (`zenoh/src/net/routing/hat/router/mod.rs` @ `.filter_map(|n| (n.is_gateway && node.links.contains_key(&n.zid)).then_some(n.zid))`): the candidates are the gateways the node ADVERTISES a link to, not the graph's edges. Nothing consumes them yet; step 5 does.

Round 2881.decision_summary:
R2881 takes open-debt item 751 step 7, the token half: liveliness tokens cross region boundaries by the pin's inter-region filter.

Measured first: of the three declaration planes the pin filters exactly one. Its dispatcher builds an `InterRegionFilter` at three sites and only one is a declaration, the token (`zenoh/src/net/routing/dispatcher/token.rs` @ `let filter = InterRegionFilter {`); subscribers and queryables propagate their `other_info` to every region unfiltered. So the population of this step is the token plane alone, and `self_advertises_sub_into` stays a bare `held_outside`.

The pin asks the filter once per destination region, with no destination node (`dst_zid: None`), per arriving declaration, passing the declaration's origin as `src_zid` and the face it arrived on as `fwd_zid`. wz's token plane is a fold: `self_advertises_token_into(target, ke)` decides whether self advertises into `target`, and the snapshot diff turns that into declares and retractions. The filter therefore goes INTO the fold, asked per origin: a mesh holder contributes only the sources whose token the filter lets cross. A broker holder contributes unfiltered, because a broker hat has no gateway view (`zenoh/src/net/routing/hat/broker/mod.rs` @ `fn gateways(&self, _tables: &TablesData) -> Option<Vec<ZenohIdProto>> {`) and a client region is south of its router, so the pin always admits it; that is R2879's reading of the same hat for the data plane.

The one structure that did not exist was the forwarder. The mesh token table keeps each origin (`LinkstatepeerInterest<()>`, keyed by source zid) but not the neighbour its declaration came through, which is what the filter reads when the source is south (`zenoh/src/net/routing/dispatcher/tables.rs` @ `.map(|fwd_zid| tables.hats[this.src].gateways_of(&tables.data, fwd_zid))`). Storing it as the table's value was measured and refused: `register` reports a change whenever the value differs, and `commit_register` re-floods on a change, so a copy of the same token arriving through a second neighbour would re-flood. The forwarder is DERIVED instead, from the graph that routed the declaration: self's parent in the source's tree (`next_hop(source, source)`), and in a gossip region, which has no tree and where declarations come from direct neighbours only, the source itself when self links to it. That is the derive-not-store idiom the tables already follow.

Undeclare needs no rule of its own. The pin's undeclare is unfiltered, but it only retracts what was propagated, and wz's before/after fold carries the filter on both sides, so a router that never advertised a token retracts nothing when it leaves; the north witness asserts both halves.

The interest half of step 7 is measured, not built. The pin's dispatcher carries three direction guards on the interest protocol that the wz router lacks: a token carrying an interest id from a south-bound face is refused (`zenoh/src/net/routing/dispatcher/token.rs` @ `if interest_id.is_some() && self.state.region.bound().is_south() {`), an interest from a north-bound non-peer is refused and one from a router ignored (`zenoh/src/net/routing/dispatcher/interests.rs` @ `if region.bound().is_north() && !self.state.whatami.is_peer() {`), and a DeclareFinal from a south-bound face is refused (`zenoh/src/net/routing/dispatcher/interests.rs` @ `error!("Received DeclareFinal from south-bound face");`). wz's router answers an Interest from any face (`respond_to_interest`). The other two `is_south` / `is_north` sites in the pin's dispatcher are the admin north-source stamp and keyexpr aliasing, not this protocol.
