Round 2882.decision_summary:
R2882 takes open-debt item 751 step 7's interest half, the one R2881's carry named: the direction the interest protocol may flow in, as the pin's dispatcher enforces it before any hat sees a message.

The population was derived from the pin's dispatcher rather than from the item's words. It holds five `is_north` / `is_south` sites; three are the interest protocol and two are not (the admin north-source stamp in `tables.rs` and keyexpr aliasing in `resource.rs`). The three:
- an `Interest` from a north-bound face unless the remote is a peer, and from any router, is refused (`zenoh/src/net/routing/dispatcher/interests.rs` @ `if region.bound().is_north() && !self.state.whatami.is_peer() {`, then `@ if self.state.whatami.is_router() {`);
- a token carrying an interest id, which is an answer, from a south-bound face is refused (`zenoh/src/net/routing/dispatcher/token.rs` @ `if interest_id.is_some() && self.state.region.bound().is_south() {`);
- a `DeclareFinal` from a south-bound face is refused (`zenoh/src/net/routing/dispatcher/interests.rs` @ `error!("Received DeclareFinal from south-bound face");`).

wz's router answered an Interest from every face and registered an interest-stamped token from every face. Both now go through one rule, `InterestFlow` (a solicitation must come from below and never from a router; an answer must come from above), read at the dispatch head with the face's region and remote mode. The third site changes no behaviour here and is not wired: this router sends no interest, so it holds no breadcrumb a `DeclareFinal` could close, and it already routed none. For the same reason the answer flow has exactly one consumer, the token, and exists with `routing-token-tables`.

One question was measured rather than assumed: whether anything in this tree relied on a router answering another router's interest. The session layer emits interests whatever its mode (publisher matching listener, querier, liveliness subscriber), so a router node's own session reaching another router over the wire would now go unanswered. The router mesh E2E suite, which runs wz routers against each other, passed 8 of 8 on this change.

Round 2885.decision_summary:
R2885 closes open-debt item 825, the census head: a wz node's identity when none is configured. R2883 paid the mesh half; this round pays the rest and closes the item.

The premise was re-measured before acting and it shrank. The register said eight E2E files expect the single-session constant `01020304`. Five of them are codec fixtures that happen to use the same bytes and have nothing to do with the demo. The other three do not expect the value at all; they work AROUND it with an explicit `--zid` and say why, one of them recording the measured consequence (`wz_unixpipe_zenohd_dataplane.rs`: two demo instances with the same zid, and zenohd refuses the second session `Terminal`).

The measurement also widened the scope. `DEMO_ZID` was not only the single-session default: the star `--router` and the storage host opened their sessions with it too, so every star router of this build was `01020304`.

The structure, not the constant, was the defect. `demo_session_init_params` SET a default zid and every run-mode that wanted another one overwrote it afterwards, so a mode that forgot to overwrite silently kept the shared identity. The rule R2883 wrote for the mesh modes (`resolve_node_zid`: the configured `--zid`, else sixteen random bytes, redrawn if zero, canonical length) moved to `args.rs`, where no feature gates it, and `demo_session_init_params` now takes the zid as a PARAMETER. No default exists any more, so each of the six callers had to choose, and the compiler enumerated them: the single-session modes, the star router, the peer, the router-hat and the storage host.

One coupling had to be kept that a naive change would have broken. The single-session modes announce their zid in four places: the Scout frame, the reconnect's re-scout, the advanced publisher's source id, and the session handshake. Each used to fall back to the constant on its own, which agreed only because it was a constant; four independent random draws would have made the Scout announce one node and the session open as another. `main` now resolves the zid once, where `--zid` is parsed, and passes that one value to all four.

The storage host's pico witness scrapes one zid across four sequential client sessions, so its zid must be stable within a process; one draw per process before the accept loop keeps that.

Round 2892.decision_summary:
R2892 repays R2888's hosted red on Layer Z (run 36265473247), and in doing so finds and fixes a stamping defect in the peer forwarder.

`wz_reads_a_stock_zenohd_config`'s relay leg stands a three-node star around the node a config file describes: a peer publisher and a peer subscriber, each reaching only that node. After R2888 the router arm read `NoInbound`: the publisher never learned the subscriber's interest, because the router no longer re-floods one peer's declaration to another peer of its region. Before changing the test, the upstream was run rather than read. A stock zenohd 1.10.0, with gossip off and no listener on either end, relays a Put from a peer to a client and not from one peer to another, both as a router and as a peer (5 samples to the client, 0 to the peer, in each mode), which is the pin's `self.region() != *src_region` in the peer hat. The star's subscriber is therefore a client now, the shape the pin relays.

That re-founded star exposed a wz defect in the PeerMesh arm: with `timestamping/enabled` on, the peer relayed the Put to the client bare. The peer forwarder stamped inside `forward_push`, which serves the mesh only, while the local subscribers, the client subscribers and the client re-inject received the unstamped Put. zenoh stamps once in `route_data`, before every direction of the route. The stamp now happens once at the Push arm of the peer's `forward`, and it is `NodeHlc::stamp_for_every_destination`, which the router forwarder calls too, so the two forwarders share one stamp point instead of two copies that had drifted. A dropped Put skips its own message only; the rest of the batch is served.

The unit witness `the_config_map_decides_whether_a_relaying_peer_stamps` now drives the Put through the ingress with a client subscriber beside the mesh one and asserts both copies carry the same stamp; with the client path fed the pre-stamp Put it is red.

The probe also showed that wz in PEER mode relays between two peers, which no zenohd does. That is item 751 applied to the peer forwarder, recorded in the register as 8e rather than built here: many peer-mesh tests assume the relay, so its population needs the same measurement 8b had.

Round 2893.decision_summary:
R2893 builds the base of open-debt item 751 rule 8d: the routing graph now knows which of the pin's two gossiping objects it stands for, and decides every topology flood shape itself.

The pin has two objects that gossip. A region's net is `Network`, and the router's south peer region builds one with `full_linkstate` off (`zenoh/src/net/routing/hat/peer/mod.rs` @ `Bound::South => {`). With link-state and multihop both off, a `Network` keeps a new link and nothing else: no node for the neighbour, no self link, no sn bump, nothing to existing links, a bootstrap of its announced direct neighbours by zid only, never self (`zenoh/src/net/protocol/network.rs` @ `if self.full_linkstate || self.gossip_multihop {`). A peer's own north region is `Gossip` (`zenoh/src/net/protocol/gossip.rs` @ `pub(crate) fn add_link`), which adds the neighbour's node and announces self. wz had one flag for both. `LinkstateNetwork` now carries the object: `new_in_region` builds a `Network`, `new` builds the peer's graph, and the single-hop rules apply only to a `Network`. `add_link` and `remove_link` follow the pin for it, and four builders take the flood decisions out of the forwarders: the new-link bootstrap, the delta to existing links, the delta on a lost link, and the re-flood of an ingest. The peer forwarder's behaviour is unchanged; holding its graph to `gossip.rs` is rule 8e.

Two defects surfaced while moving the decisions, and both were repaired at the shared point. The router's per-region re-flood withheld the whole list from the source face, the defect R311y431 had found and fixed on the peer side only: psid space is per sender, so the source must get the new node back. And source resolution demanded a graph node to number the source by, which a single-hop `Network` does not have for a neighbour that has not yet announced itself, so a peer's first declaration was dropped. The source zid is now resolved on its own (the pin's `remote_node_id_to_zid` reads the link, not the graph), and the relay psid is optional where nothing is relayed.

The south net is NOT switched off in this round, and that is a measurement, not a deferral. With it off, 18 router unit tests went red and were driven to 4 by the two repairs above plus re-founding; but three router-hat mesh E2Es went red, because wz's own peers default to the link-state peer mode the pin deleted, and a link-state peer's ingest collects every link-less gossip entry as detached. A peer mode must be the same across a subsystem. The switch therefore lands with rule 8e, which makes wz's peer the pin's peer, in one round. The four re-founded tests are kept as that round's population.

Witnesses: a graph test puts a single-hop `Network` and a peer graph through the same links and checks each answers as its pin object (red with the object test disabled); a router test checks the source face gets the new node back (red with the source withheld).

Round 2895.decision_summary:
R2895 builds the structure open-debt item 751 rule 8e was missing: a routing link now carries its far end's bound, and a peer's single-hop gossip graph reads its flood decisions off it as the pin's `Gossip` object does.

The pin keeps the remote bound on every link of a peer's `Gossip` (`zenoh/src/net/protocol/gossip.rs` @ `pub(crate) fn add_link`) and decides three things from it: a neighbour is a gateway when its bound is south (`zenoh/src/net/protocol/gossip.rs` @ `is_gateway: remote_bound.is_south(),`), a link-added change is sent only to such links (`zenoh/src/net/protocol/gossip.rs` @ `.filter(|link| link.zid != zid && link.remote_bound.is_south())`), and a new link's bootstrap carries self's links only toward one (`zenoh/src/net/protocol/gossip.rs` @ `links: remote_bound.is_south(),`). The gateway bit therefore comes from the transport, not from link-state. wz's `Link` held a zid and nothing else, so none of the three could be expressed.

The bound is the one the pin stores on the face: announced by the far end, or else derived from the two roles (`zenoh/src/net/runtime/region.rs` @ `fn compute_auto_region(`). Under the default preset nobody announces one, so for a peer the derivation is what matters: a router it links to is south, a peer is north. wz already had that computation as `region_and_bound_of`; both forwarders now pass its answer to the graph through `add_link_bound`, and `add_link` keeps its meaning of a link with no south bound. The graph applies the three rules only to a peer's graph in single-hop gossip; a region's `Network` and every link-state graph read none of them.

This changes what a wz peer in gossip mode sends: a sibling peer is no longer bootstrapped with links, and an existing sibling link no longer hears a link-added change. The three zenohd interop targets that run wz peers in that mode pass against a local zenohd (11 tests).

The default peer mode is unchanged in this round; retiring the link-state peer mode and switching the router's south net off together remain rule 8e's next step.

R2896 lands the switch open-debt item 751 had been building towards: a wz peer and the peer region of a wz router now run the pin's gossip mode by default, and the router's peer region follows its peers when they are told otherwise.

The pin has one peer mode. Its peer hat builds a region's net with `full_linkstate` false (`zenoh/src/net/routing/hat/peer/mod.rs` @ `Bound::South => {`), and the key that used to choose is deprecated without effect. wz defaulted its peers to the link-state mode the pin deleted, and kept its router's peer region on link-state to match. R2893 measured why the two cannot move apart: with the router's region switched alone, three router-hat mesh E2Es went red, because a link-state peer's ingest collects every link-less gossip entry as detached. A mode has to be the same across a subsystem. With both switched, all eight of those E2Es pass.

The config reader's default for the key and the expansion's direction flip with the default: `peer-to-peer` is now the value that states the default, and `linkstate` the one that earns the flag.

Round 2897.decision_summary:
R2897 corrects a claim R2893 wrote and repairs the defect the correction exposed: in the pin, which locators a link-state entry carries is decided per node on every send, never by the entry's form.

R2893 wrote into `build_new_link_bootstrap`'s doc that the pin's new-link bootstrap carries no locators while wz's does, and registered that as a divergence. Checked against the pin before re-grading `routing-router`, it is the other way round. The pin's send overwrites whatever locator choice its caller made with one per-node gate (`zenoh/src/net/protocol/network.rs` @ `idx.1.locators = self.propagate_locators(idx.0, transport);`): self and direct neighbours carry theirs, every node does under multihop, and the caller's `Details` never decides it. So the pin's bootstrap does carry them. wz let the entry's form decide, carrying locators on the full form only, which dropped them from forms the pin sends them on: self's links-only update, a neighbour's zid-only introduction on a new link, the single-hop `Network`'s bootstrap. A separate zid-plus-locators form existed only to put them back for the gossip re-flood.

`make_link_state` now applies the per-node gate on every form, `Details` loses its locator column and that extra form, and the doc carries the correction. The per-target half of the pin's gate stays with the driver's fan-out, as before. A witness puts self, a direct neighbour and a distant node side by side: the first two carry locators on the links-only and zid-only forms and the third is withheld even on the full form; with the old rule restored it is red on self's update. The zenohd interop targets that dial off learned locators pass unchanged. A doc link to the removed form left the graph crate's public docs, so its C1bz budget falls from 6 to 5.

R2900 builds the residual R2899 re-measured: the mesh dial refused the four endpoint shapes with no socket address (`serial`, `unixsock-stream`, `unixpipe`, `vsock`) because its loop keyed a dial target by that address, while the pin connects over any endpoint through one path in every mode. The fix is at the base, the key: a dial target is now keyed by the endpoint's own identity, `MeshDialKey`, so every machinery that was keyed by address (the desired set, the dialed-target map, the re-dial schedule, the reconcile channel, the multilink re-add, the gossip dial intent) carries the new key, and the population was taken from the compiler, not from a list. `mesh_dial_plan` now refuses exactly one shape, an unresolved name, which the resolver step turns into an address before the plan is asked.

`routing-router` returns to COMPLETE: that was its one residual, and a wz router dialling a stock zenohd over `unixsock-stream` is its witness. `routing-peer`'s dial clause closes too, but building its witness found the residual that stands: a pin peer not mutually north-bound with its gateway sends its interests to that gateway and pulls the declarations behind it, and the wz peer sends none, so a peer attached to a router receives nothing from the router's other clients. That is registered as open-debt item 828, and the peer witness stays face-level until it is built. REMAINING falls from 13 to 12.

Reading the hosted runs at the round's start found one red in a completed run: R2896's switch of the peer default to gossip left `wz_peer_qabl_pico_interop` waiting on a link-state edge a gossip net never forms, while its query crossed the mesh. Its barrier moves to the ingest witness, the R2236 precedent; the population of tests waiting on that edge was derived by search, and the only other live waiter already forces link-state.

carry_forward_bullets: Last residual of `routing-peer` (open-debt item 828): the finalized withhold. Round 2903.decision_summary: Round 2903 closes R2902's delivery gap for `routing-peer` (open-debt item 828). A pico publisher attached to a wz peer that sits under a stock router now reaches a subscriber behind the router. The base was the interest broker (atom `routing-interest-pending-gc`), which was narrower than the pin's plane-agnostic `route_interest` in three ways. It brokered only token interests. It sent every copy as a token interest. And it relayed the upstream's answers verbatim, so a keyexpr scope that meant something only on the upstream link reached the client. Two live traces refined the design. First, zenohd answers under a link alias whenever asked for keyexprs. Second, a gateway strips a peer's AGGREGATE bit and leaves aggregation to the client-facing node. The shape built is the pin's: forward the client's options, ingest the gateway's subscriber and queryable answers as its declarations, answer the client from this node's tables, and broker only the final. `routing-peer` stays PARTIAL on the finalized withhold, which this round makes buildable by recording the gateway's answers under the gateway.

Round 2907.decision_summary: Round 2907 works open-debt item 829 in the order its prescription names: before the `RouteTable` engine can be retired, sort which of its 63 C1x tests have a counterpart on the router hat that `--router` actually runs. The sort (34 covered, 15 partial, 14 none) turned up two defects in the hat itself, and a defect outranks a missing test, so this round repairs them at their base. Round 2918.decision_summary: Round 2918 builds `platform-zephyr`'s last two residuals and re-grades it COMPLETE (REMAINING 9 -> 8). THE RNG SEAM: `ZephyrEntropy` implements the session core's `EntropySource` over a board hook, `wzApplicationGetRandom`, which the board serves from `sys_rand_get` -- pico's `z_random_fill`. It is a hook and not FFI because neither kernel route is nameable: `sys_rand_get` is a `__syscall` wrapper with no link symbol, and the real `getentropy` requires an entropy DEVICE, which a TRNG-less board such as QEMU mps2/an385 does not have. THE EPOCH SEAM: `ZephyrEpoch` implements `EpochSource` over `wzApplicationGetTimeSinceEpoch`, the very hook and contract the FreeRTOS profile reads, so one board-side answer serves either RTOS; the board serves it from `clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME)`, pico's `_z_get_time_since_epoch`, and the hook names fixed-width integers because `struct timespec`'s `time_t` width is the C library's. The QEMU board has no RTC, so `main()` sets the realtime clock to the build's own instant at boot, standing in for an SNTP sync -- a named fixture, as its test random generator is. The image's session now draws its cookie nonce and signing key through `ZephyrEntropy` (3 board draws) and mints an NTP64 through `ZephyrEpoch`. THE ATOM'S REACH is now real: crate tests stand in the kernel tick and both hooks with statics and name `ZephyrClock`, `ZephyrEntropy` and `ZephyrEpoch`, where R2916's census reading was a method-name collision (item 831). Round 2919.decision_summary: Round 2919 opens `transport-qos` (PARTIAL), chosen after re-measuring the milestone's candidates: its three residuals share ONE base, and that base is buildable here. Before choosing, the hosted reds were re-measured rather than inherited: runs 36316772299 (R2908's tip), 36317861701 (R2909's) and 36321180514 (R2910's) show failed jobs, and every failing gate traces to two causes -- the `FaceMap` dead-code compile error under reduced features and the C1y `linkstate` count -- both already repaid on HEAD by R2910-R2912; the failing commands re-run on HEAD pass (the C4 ap-router preset builds, the C1bn `session_lifecycle_open` leg runs 4, C1bl runs 1, C1y linkstate prints 223, its guard). THE BASE: the atom's residuals are (1) priority orders frames only inside a batch window, (2) no per-priority queue depth, (3) no drop-vs-block congestion -- and each waits on the same fact, that wz had no priority-ordered TX queue. The AP already hands frames to a writer task, but over one unbounded FIFO channel, and the link seam (`BoxedLinkDriver::send_blocking`) received bytes and a reliability only, so a frame's band decided its header byte and never when it left. zenoh's transmission pipeline keeps a queue per priority and its consumer pulls the lowest non-empty first. This round builds that ordering: the writer channel is now `writer_queue::outbound_channel`, one FIFO lane per `Priority` drained in strict ascending order (FIFO within a lane keeps each conduit's SN order), every AP pipeline (the six byte-stream ones, udp, ws, quic-datagram, serial) enqueues on it, and the session hands each frame to the link through a new seam, `BoxedLinkDriver::send_prioritized`, at the frame's own priority; MCU drivers keep the default, which writes synchronously. Control frames follow upstream's choices, measured at the pin: a keepalive at `Priority::Control` (zenoh's tx task writes it directly, ahead of queued batches) and a close at `Priority::Background`, behind queued data, so data sent before a close leaves first. A non-QoS session still sends every data frame at `Priority::DEFAULT`, so its data is one FIFO lane, as zenoh's single-queue pipeline is. Residual (1) is therefore closed at the queue: a higher-priority frame overtakes lower ones already handed to the writer, batch window or not. STILL OPEN: (2) the lanes are unbounded, so there is no depth to report, and (3) with no bound there is no congestion; both are next, and (3) must decide BEFORE the SN mint or restore the SN as zenoh does, since a drop at the link would leave a gap.

Round 2920.decision_summary: Round 2920 builds the base `transport-qos`'s congestion residual stands on: a TX lock per priority conduit. The session had ONE TX lock, `tx_mutex`, guarding every priority's batch stage and serializing every sender -- the SN mint and the wire emit under one hold. zenoh locks per priority (`io/zenoh-transport/src/common/pipeline.rs` @ `// Each priority queue has its own Mutex`), and the next round needs exactly that: once a full lane makes a sender wait for room (droppable up to `wait_before_drop`, blocking up to `wait_before_close`), a wait under a session-wide lock would stall every priority behind a congested Background one, which is the failure zenoh's per-priority stage lock exists to prevent. Nothing needs the wider lock: a conduit's SN ring, its open batch frame and its fragment chains are its own, and no invariant spans two conduits (the effective priority is resolved before the lock, and a non-QoS session is forced onto the DEFAULT conduit there). `tx_mutex` is now `TxConduits`: one `BatchTx` behind its own lock per priority (one without `transport-qos`), and the batching window flag as an atomic, since the window spans every conduit and no conduit's lock may stand for the others. The emit chokepoint locks its message's conduit; the batch drain walks the conduits in ascending band, each under its own hold, so a conduit's frames keep their SN order; the reopen reset clears each. The witness drives the property rather than the structure: a link write that stalls on Background, a Background send stalled inside it holding its conduit's lock, and a RealTime send that must complete meanwhile; collapsing every conduit onto one lock reds it. Round 2921.decision_summary: Round 2921 bounds the link writer's priority lanes, the second base `transport-qos`'s congestion residual needs (R2919 ordered the lanes, R2920 gave each conduit its own TX lock). zenoh bounds each priority queue by a pool of `queue_size` batches -- 2 per band at the pin (`commons/zenoh-config/src/defaults.rs` @ `impl Default for QueueSizeConf {`) -- and a producer that finds no free batch waits for the tx task to return one. wz's lanes were unbounded, so no sender could ever find one full. THE UNIT is the decision this round had to make, and it is BYTES: wz hands its writer frames, and outside a batch window each network message is its own frame, where zenoh's always-on batching coalesces a burst of small messages into one batch; a bound of 2 FRAMES would congest a burst zenoh absorbs. So a lane holds `queue_size * batch_bytes` (2 x 65535, zenoh's `BatchSize::MAX`), which is the room zenoh's batches hold. A frame occupies its lane from enqueue until the writer asks for the next frame, which is when the one it held has been written, as zenoh returns a batch to the pool only after the write. `OutboundTx::wait_for_room(priority, wait)` is zenoh's "wait for an available batch until deadline" -- Free, Congested (the lane stayed full for the whole wait) or Closed -- and reaches the session through a new link seam, `BoxedLinkDriver::wait_for_room(priority, wait_us) -> LinkRoom`, which every AP write driver answers from its queue and the synchronous MCU drivers answer Free by default. It is asked BEFORE a frame is built, so a sender that gives up has minted no SN. `send` still always enqueues: the frames that must never wait (a keepalive, a close) take it as they are. NOTHING CALLS the room seam yet; the session's decision -- a droppable message dropped after `wait_before_drop`, a blocking one closing the link after `wait_before_close`, both before the mint -- is the next round.

Round 2923.decision_summary: Round 2923 makes `transport-qos`'s congestion decision, on the two bases R2921 (bounded lanes) and R2922 (out-of-band requests reach the loop) built. Before a data frame's sequence number is minted, the session asks the link its conduit is routed to for room: a droppable message (best effort, or `CongestionControl::Drop`, read off the message's OWN ext_qos in each of the seven dispatchers) waits `wait_before_drop` (1 ms) and, finding none, is dropped with no sequence number spent; a blocking one waits `wait_before_close` (5 s) and then stages a congestion close that `drive::check_out_of_band` raises as `tx.congestion.exhaust`, closing the session UNRESPONSIVE as zenoh's `handle_push_result` does. Measuring the inherited draft against upstream found a missing piece: zenoh marks a priority queue CONGESTED when a push gives up, and while the mark stands a droppable message is dropped WITHOUT waiting; the mark clears when the consumer returns a batch. The mark lives with the queue, so the link seam now says which kind of message is asking -- `wait_for_room(priority, RoomWait::{Drop, Block})` -- and each writer lane carries the mark. A congestion drop counts as `n_dropped` and not `n_msgs` (upstream's `tx_n_dropped` IS the congestion count), so the legacy `n_msgs` moved from entry to push, as its registry twin already had. Measuring the seam's population found a join defect: the reconnect swap seams (`SwappableLink`, `LocalSwappableLink`) forwarded only a frame's bytes, so from R2919 a reconnecting session's frames reached its link at the default priority and could never congest; they now forward the priority, the room and the MTU. Round 2926.decision_summary: Round 2926 builds `transport-qos`'s fragment-chain congestion: a chain now asks its conduit's link for room before EACH fragment, against the message's ONE deadline, as upstream's chain waits for a batch per fragment. Upstream's deadline is an instant: `wait_before_drop` for a droppable message, extended after each fragment by an increment that doubles, all extensions capped together by `max_wait_before_drop_fragments`; a blocking message has no cap, so its chain shares one `wait_before_close`. The session has no clock that fine (its `TimeSource` counts milliseconds, and the first wait is one), so it holds the deadline as microseconds LEFT, spent by what each ask reports it waited: `BoxedLinkDriver::wait_for_room` now answers a `RoomAnswer { room, waited_us }`, measured in the writer queue, which is where the waiting happens and where a `std` clock is. `PushDeadline` mirrors upstream's `WaitTime::advance` step for step. A chain that runs out part-way is abandoned the way a spent fragment budget already abandoned it here: the stop fragment carrying the Drop extension 0x3, on the next sequence number, outside the queue's bound as upstream's ephemeral batch is outside its pool, and the message is a congestion drop that closes the session when it may not be dropped. `max_wait_before_drop_fragments` is therefore honoured, through the same path R2925 laid for the other ten. Also found: R2924 wired the swap seams to forward the queue shape and nothing exercised it; the forwarding witness now does, together with the full room answer. Round 2927.decision_summary: Round 2927 closes `transport-qos`'s non-QoS priority divergence, and in measuring it found two defects where the reason named one. Upstream refuses a Frame or Fragment carrying a non-DEFAULT priority over a transport that negotiated no QoS as a LINK error: its rx task bails, and the transport deletes the link, closing it with no Close message and deleting the transport when it was the last link. wz dropped such a frame and kept the link -- and it checked only in `transport-qos` builds, though the priority is decoded in every build, so a build without the feature admitted a prioritized frame onto its one conduit. Both arms now refuse in every build through the session's `link.lost` path (`LostCause::UnknownPriority`): Closed, the link released through `release_link` (which removes it from a multilink set and closes its driver, as upstream's `del_link` does), no Close sent -- not `framing.error`, which would send Close(Invalid). Round 2928.decision_summary: Round 2928 lays the base of `transport-qos`'s last named residual, the multicast per-priority pipeline, in `wz-session-core`, and answers the question the carry put first: the room check sits BEFORE the sequence-number mint, on the producer's side of a bounded queue, as upstream's pipeline asks for a batch under its stage lock before it serializes (`io/zenoh-transport/src/common/pipeline.rs` @ `pub(crate) fn push_network_message(`). `multicast_tx_push` asks a `MulticastTxQueue` for room with the message's `PushDeadline` (`wait_before_drop` for a droppable message, `wait_before_close` for a blocking one), mints only once it has room, and streams an oversize frame as a fragment chain that asks again before each further fragment, stopping a chain that runs out with a drop marker on the next SN, as the unicast chain does since R2926. `Congested` is the whole of what multicast does with such a message: upstream's multicast schedule counts it and closes nothing (`io/zenoh-transport/src/multicast/tx.rs` @ `fn schedule_on_link(&self, msg: NetworkMessageRef) -> ZResult<bool> {`). No runtime uses the bounded path yet: the AP loop still drains an unbounded item channel and is the only task that both receives and sends, so a reply its own RX produces would wait on a queue only it drains. Round 2929.decision_summary:
ZA-3214 items 4 and 3 of four, landed first so the field document's revision 13 is settled before the two larger items that also move it.

Item 4 is a defect repaid. The selector door has written `selected` with four words (yes, no, undecided, unjudged) on every row since R2766, and no revision named the key and no family held the words. R2175's contract is that a closed vocabulary a consumer switches on is declared, with an `@values` marker in the header and a row in `value_families`. So a consumer's switch over these words had nothing to pin, and nothing in this tree would have broken on a fifth word. The fix makes the four words ONE type (`fields_json::RowVerdict`), declares field-document revision 13 with the key, the family and its carries axis (passenger), and marks the header.

Item 3 carries the lexer's tokens on the selector verdict. A consumer colouring a selector as it is typed kept a lexer of its own next to this one, and two lexers over one language eventually disagree about where a token begins. The verdict now closes, on BOTH branches, with `tokens`: a byte span (`start`, `end` exclusive, the same unit `at` uses) and a `kind` from a closed set of eight (word, quoted, operator, not, and, or, open, close). It is the same walk `Filter::parse` runs, and on a LEXICAL failure it keeps every token before the failure, so the colouring survives an unclosed quote. `kind` stops at the lexer's own distinctions: whether a word is a field or a value is the parser's knowledge, and the parser may never reach a token the lexer produced. Selector-verdict revision 2 declares the family.

Neither item adds a symbol, so the ABI revision does not move. For keys and values the document revision is the notice.

A consuming viewer reported that wz judges four things per frame and hands none of them over, so it rebuilt them as indexes of its own: the reassembly router's outcome per Fragment and which rows share a chain, the SN verdict and the conduit it was judged on, the flow's negotiated context, and where a row's first byte sits in the capture. All four were measured to exist inside the reader already -- `PassiveFrame::sn_verdict`, `Carried::Fragment(IngestOutcome)`, `FlowContext`, the stream assembler's offset runs -- so the round is plumbing to the field document, not new judgement.

DECIDED -- the chain identity follows the ROUTER'S OWN KEY, not the rows. The router keys a chain by (peer, reliable, priority) and an observer holds one router per direction, so the fold keys on (direction, reliable, priority) read off the same Fragment fields and advances on the router's outcome alone: `begun` always mints, because a `First` restart and a deadline sweep both end the open chain WITHOUT a row. Folded ahead of the listing cap, so an identity never renumbers when the cap moves. It is an identity for ROWS; the joined buffer's offsets stay off the document for R2706's reason.

DECIDED -- chains that end with no row are counted, not inferred. The capture report's `reassembly` group (expired / abandoned_at_end / abandoned_on_eviction) was lifted into one emitter and the field document carries it at the top level. The C library had no door to that count before: the summary's health `fragments` object is IP-fragment reassembly, a different fact.

DECIDED -- the frame offset is located by walking the SAME doors decapsulate walks, with the TCP and UDP header rules shared between the strips and the locator, rather than by threading a field through Segment and Datagram (owned payloads, many constructors that could not fill it). A WebSocket row answers null: its coordinate names the ws frame header and the message sits past it, masked.

Round 2933.decision_summary:
A consuming viewer asked for both halves of R2930's fifth item to be BUILT: lz4 in the dissection build, and a door returning a reassembled row's joined buffer.

MEASURED FIRST, AND IT CHANGED THE ROUND. Turning the feature on was not the fix. The observer decompressed a `Frame`'s PAYLOAD on a compression-negotiated session, and that is not where upstream compresses. Read at the pinned source. The sender reserves a one-byte BatchHeader ahead of the batch and lz4s everything behind it:
`io/zenoh-transport/src/common/batch.rs` @ `fn compress(&mut self, support: &mut BBuf)`
The receiver reads that header and decompresses the whole payload before it decodes one message:
`io/zenoh-transport/src/common/batch.rs` @ `let zslice = self.decompress(p, buff)?;`
Each side switches its link to compression once IT has sent its Open:
`io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/establishment/open.rs` @ `is_compression: state.link.ext_compression.is_compression(),`
The OpenAck is sent with compression off:
`io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/link.rs` @ `pub(crate) async fn send_open_ack(mut self)`
The lowlatency transport writes messages with no batch and no header at all:
`io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/lowlatency/link.rs` @ `pub(crate) async fn send_with_link(`
wz's own participant already wraps at the batch; only the observer did not.

RED FIRST, AND BOTH PROOFS ARE RECORDED. With `compression` enabled on the old model, an upstream-shaped lz4 batch yielded no record, and R2706's own marker fixture stopped reporting undecompressible because its four bytes "decompressed" as a raw payload. After the repair, forcing the header step off reddens exactly the six tests that read a compressed batch.

DECIDED -- the header is found per direction, on the same switch lowlatency's width uses (`FlowContext::batch_header_active`: negotiated, compression, not lowlatency, Established, and this direction's own Open seen). A clear header is stepped over and the batch read in WIRE coordinates, so every row still points at the capture. A set header is opened through the participant's own `compression::decompress_batch`, bounded by MAX_FRAME_PAYLOAD. A decompressed message carries its own bytes (`PassiveFrame::decompressed`), because its coordinate indexes a buffer the walk drops; `batch_offset` and the field row's `first_byte` are null for it. A batch that does not open is ONE record, `CompressionFailed` / `Carried::Undecompressible`, and its bytes are unaccounted, by the rule an undecodable datagram already follows. `CompressionFailed` is ungated so every build can say it.

DECIDED -- `compression` is a wz-capture feature forwarding `wz-session-core/transport-compression`, default-off for `dissect`'s reason (a third-party dependency the MCU profiles must not carry), and wz-capi-dissect selects it. The feature reaches the reader through wz-session-core; wz-capture is where it is named because it is the reader both desktop consumers compose and the crate whose tests grade it.

DECIDED -- the door is `wz_dissect_live_reassembled_bytes(h, record, out, cap, needed)`, ABI 18 -> 19. Round 2937.decision_summary: Round 2937 moves the multicast push to the PRODUCER, the base R2935's carry named. Until now an application's publish, the router's group sink and the reply sink handed their `MulticastTxItem` to the drive loop over an unbounded channel and returned, and the loop pushed; so a blocking publish never blocked and the channel in front of the bounded lanes had no bound at all. Upstream's producer pushes into the link's pipeline on its own thread and waits there (`io/zenoh-transport/src/multicast/tx.rs` @ `fn schedule_on_link(&self, msg: NetworkMessageRef) -> ZResult<bool> {`): it reads the transport's link, clones the pipeline out and lets the read go, pushes under the lock of one priority's stage (`io/zenoh-transport/src/common/pipeline.rs` @ `pub(crate) fn push_network_message(`), and drops the message when there is no link. `MulticastTxProducer` is that handle. Each of its clones pushes on the caller's thread; the pipeline it pushes onto is attached by the drive loop when the link comes up (`MulticastTxPlane::open`) and detached when it goes, so a group face that rejoins attaches a new pipeline to the same producer, and a push while nothing is attached is refused as `Unlinked`. The pipeline holds one lock per conduit, each over that conduit's minter and its record of queued SNs, so a band waiting for room holds no other band. The egress namespace is taken from the dispatcher when the pipeline is attached (`set_namespace` is already required before bring-up), so egress and ingress still come from one value. What each push did returns to the loop over a channel, because the stats recorder is the loop's and borrowed. In `wz-session-core` the push's QoS reading became one function (`frame_meta`) that the producer also asks for the conduit to lock (`multicast_tx_conduit`), and minting goes through `MulticastTxMint`, so a push runs against the one conduit held (`MulticastTxConduit`), which refuses a mint on any other band. `MulticastTxTap` attaches a pipeline with no link under it and reads what producers queued; the tests of producers read the wire bytes through it rather than a queued item. Grade unchanged (PARTIAL).

Round 2941.decision_summary: session-extqos 의 첫 잔여(FIELD-IDENTITY: wz 는 band 원천이 둘, zenoh 는 하나)를 base 에서 닫는다. 상류의 `prio=` endpoint metadata 는 wire offer 이자 link.config.priorities 인 한 필드다. wz 의 multilink 배포 split 은 egress 슬롯에 직접 쓰이고 광고되지 않아, 협상한 band 와 routing 하는 band 가 달랐다. 수리는 split 을 «dialled 링크의 QoSLink offer» 로 staging 하는 것(운영자가 band 를 설정했으면 그것이 우선)이고, accepted 끝은 운영자 설정만 선언하고 dialler 의 band 를 채택한다 — 상류 acceptor 는 수락된 링크 자신의 src endpoint 에서 seed 하는데 TCP 는 그 metadata 를 비워 둔다(`io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/establishment/accept.rs` @ `let endpoint = link.get_src().to_endpoint();`, `io/zenoh-links/zenoh-link-tcp/src/unicast.rs` @ `src_locator: Locator::new(TCP_LOCATOR_PREFIX, src_addr.to_string(), "")`). acceptor 도 자기 split 을 선언하는 대안은 기각: 양끝이 face id 를 각자 매기므로 parity 가 어긋나는 흔한 경우마다 containment 가 subset 아님으로 handshake 를 abort 한다. band 가 한 원천이 되자 write-back 의 None arm 이 이제 상류와 같이 충실하다: 협상 결과는 None 포함 항상 egress band 에 쓰이고, NoQoS 경로도 상태와 band 를 비운다(`io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/establishment/ext/qos.rs` @ `*state_self = State::NoQoS.into();`). 같은 seam 의 잔여를 같은 라운드에: 쿠키/재개가 되돌려 주는 협상 상태(`install_negotiated`)도 슬롯만 쓰고 egress band 는 안 썼다 — 이제 두 writer 가 하나의 `settle_qos_link` 를 지난다. session-extqos 는 PARTIAL 유지: reliability 절반(`LinkReliabilityPref::Any` 대 상류의 intrinsic class 폴백, 그리고 multilink 가 face 마다 주는 미광고 reliability class)이 남은 잔여다.

Round 2942.decision_summary: Round 2942 answers ZA-3308: a one-shot --connect client of wz-ap-demo dialled once whatever connect/timeout_ms said, and the config expansion reported the key withheld, so a lab client started before its router exited where a zenohd client with timeout_ms -1 waits. The premise that withheld it, that a one-shot client never re-dials, held only of the client DEFAULT: upstream's client runs a startup connect phase whose budget decides whether it re-dials. That client now runs the phase through the runtime's drive_phase, the loop the mesh arms run, with dial and handshake as one attempt, and the expansion hands it connect/timeout_ms and connect/retry. connect/exit_on_failure stays withheld from a client, because upstream's client connect never reads it. The same reading corrects R2936: z_open had released a client whose exit_on_failure was false before its peer connected, which upstream never does, and now releases only a peer or router.

carry_forward_bullets: api-compat-c toward COMPLETE, remaining in order: (1) item 835, the unicast BlockFirst slot. Design measured: the send runs synchronously on the caller's thread down to dispatch_network_message (wz-session-core session_actions); replies run on the drive task, where a slot wait would stall inbound processing. session-core's Runtime abstraction has no wait/notify primitive; the only blocking wait it reaches is BoxedLinkDriver::wait_for_room, implemented in wz-runtime-tokio's writer_queue with a std Condvar (and block_in_place on a multi-thread runtime). So the slot is a new link-driver capability of the same shape (acquire-with-timeout per priority, release), a miss is a congestion drop that does not close the session, and the blocking push after acquisition is handed to the runtime (WzRuntime::spawn_blocking exists, citing upstream's spawn_blocking). Multicast needs no slot (parity). (2) cancellation tokens wired into get / querier / liveliness get. (3) the 8 SHM symbols that need no payload path. Round 2949.decision_summary: Round 2949 (built as R2948; another session landed its own Round 2948 - seven pico connect-phase leftovers - while this one was in flight, so this round was re-applied on top of it and renumbered, code comments included) pays api-compat-c's cancellation-token gap at its base rather than at the instance. The gap as the audit named it was "the zenoh-c option slots are void* and ignored"; measured, the structure was two cancellation models: the pico ABI had the real plane (a token with a take-once on-cancel handler list, and a per-face undo fan its gets registered into), the zenoh-c ABI a bare shared flag nothing consulted. And the pico model itself diverged from BOTH upstreams on one point: neither waited for a cancelled get's callbacks. zenoh's cancel runs the handlers then waits on a sync group every registered query holds a notifier of until its callback drops, and zenoh-pico's _z_cancellation_token_cancel does the same (_z_sync_group_wait after the handler run); a completed query also removes its handler. So the base is one token in wz-capi-core with upstream's contract (registration refused once cancel has started, a Registration dropped by the query's callbacks, cancel = run handlers outside the lock then wait for every live registration, is_cancelled once handlers ran), both ABIs on it, and the zenoh-c get / querier get / liveliness get slots typed, taken on every path, and registered - failing with Z_EGENERIC on an already-cancelled token, upstream's answer. Two findings came out of verifying it against real implementations rather than against wz. (1) Rust 2021 disjoint closure capture: a callback naming per_face.closure and per_face.gate captured only those fields, so the registration dropped at once and the handler vanished before any cancel; the pico differential (wz vs libzenohpico) redded on exactly that, and both ABIs now hold the struct whole through a &self fire method. (2) The zenoh-c differential, first written with one session and a session-local queryable, showed wz's local get finalising before a C queryable that holds the query has run (upstream keeps the get open): a local-query-plane divergence, registered as item 836 and kept out of the cancellation claim by moving legC to two sessions. An intermediate claim this round made was also refuted and is recorded: the pico cancellation differential is NOT laneless - Layer E's --ignored sweep runs it; a name search cannot see a sweep.

Round 2952.decision_summary: Round 2952 schedules a BlockFirst unicast message as zenoh 1.10.1 does, closing open-debt item 835. The schedule lives once, in dispatch_network_message, where all seven send arms meet: after the availability gate and the lowlatency return, as upstream schedules after link selection and its lowlatency transport has no block-first. The core picks the link, the wait (wait_before_drop) and the slot key (the message's own priority); the link driver waits, since the sans-IO core cannot block. A granted message's body is encoded once into a BlockFirstJob and handed to the runtime, which pushes it off the sender and then gives the slot back; a refused one is a congestion drop on the same counter as a message that found no room. A runtime with no hand-off sends block-first as blocking.

Round 2960.decision_summary:
A consumer that attaches each config-verdict reason to the config field it is about could not use the C verdict doors, and asked for two things: the key path as its own value beside the reason for a config the reader refuses, and, for a set of nodes, the node under the name the caller gave it instead of the position it was passed at. Both facts were already fields in the domain types (ConfigIngestError::path, TopologyDefect::node, endpoint, nodes) and were flattened into one sentence at the C boundary, which the header tells callers not to parse.

The round answers with NEW doors and leaves the prose doors byte-identical. Changing the prose doors would have broken every caller that splits on the colon, and the string is the stable-name-plus-prose contract the header already states.

Domain first. zenoh_config_finding turns each of ConfigDefect, TopologyDefect and ConfigIngestError into a Finding: variant name, prose, endpoint, and a list of BlamedSites, each a node and a key path. The blame is an exhaustive match with no wildcard, so a variant added later does not compile until it says what it blames, and a test holds every blamed key against HONOURED_CONFIG_KEYS. Two defect types changed shape to stop losing facts: the three endpoint defects gain the list they were read from (a string found in both lists blames both keys, not a guess), and NoNodeAccepts now carries the nodes it is about. validate_labelled_topology takes caller names; validate_topology_with_external delegates to it, so there is one body.

The C shape is a handle read a column at a time, not a JSON string and not a result struct. An accessor per column makes a future column a new symbol, which capi_c_abi_pin.py already watches, where a string or a struct would move a contract the pin cannot see. The table is flat, one row per finding and place, with the finding index so a caller can group rows back into defects. A refusal is a row as well as a return code, and the set door reports every refusal in the call rather than the first, under the names the caller gave.

Round 2962.decision_summary: Round 2962 builds pico's write filter under api-compat-pico's publisher and querier, the residual item 841 named after Round 2959 made the declarations agree. zenoh-pico 1.10.1 creates a filter for every publisher and querier (_z_write_filter_create in src/net/filtering.c): it asks its peer whether anyone matches the entity's key, starts ACTIVE, and while it is active z_publisher_put, z_publisher_delete and z_querier_get send nothing. wz sent every put and every get. The session now holds a matching Interest per filter (MatchingInterestHold, refcounted and shared with a matching listener on the same key, released on drop), each face replays the held filters when it comes up, and write_filter_active answers from the remote subscriber and queryable declarations alone, so a local declaration never opens a filter. The pico ABI keeps a WriteFilter on every PublisherState and QuerierState and consults it first; a client asks aggregated over the alias id the entity's declared key already owns, a peer asks only when it has a router peer, exactly as _z_add_interest does. The differential that pinned the residual on both sides now compares the whole client arm and passes: the two arms agree line for line, including the Interest per publisher and querier, its Final on undeclare, and the Query a querier withholds with no matching queryable. Behaviour shrinks on purpose, as upstream does: a put with no remote subscriber is not sent.

Round 2964.decision_summary: Round 2964 repays the first of api-compat-pico's two standing cost divergences at its base, after measuring it. The atom's reason and the crate's own docs said z_bytes_from_static_str copies where zenoh-pico aliases and called that "confined to cost, not to observable behaviour"; z_string_from_str and its siblings were recorded with "one observable consequence", the deleter running at construction. A new compile-twice probe (pico_bytes_alias_twice_and_diff) ran one C program against the real libzenohpico and against wz and found the record wrong in both directions of size and kind: 24 of 92 lines differed, across the whole family and not one constructor. In the real library every constructor that takes a caller's buffer (z_bytes_from_static_str, z_bytes_from_static_buf, z_bytes_from_buf, z_bytes_from_str, z_slice_from_buf, z_string_from_str) describes it, so the view pointer is the caller's pointer and a change made through that pointer shows in the payload; the caller's deleter runs once, when the last holder is dropped; z_bytes_from_slice and z_bytes_from_string take over the allocation they are given; z_bytes_clone shares its storage even for an owned payload; only z_slice_clone, z_string_clone and z_bytes_to_slice copy. wz's payload was an owning Vec with a deep-copying Clone, so none of that was reachable. The base is that model, not any one constructor: ByteBuf now holds an Arc over a Backing that is either an owned Vec or the caller's bytes plus a Release that runs the caller's deleter on drop, clone shares, extraction copies by name, and a writer that must change shared or aliased bytes copies them first. Slices and strings hold the same Backing, so a move into a payload shares the allocation and the deleter waits for both. The measurement also found a type pun in a unit test that had read a ByteBuf handle as a Vec because its first field happened to be one; it now reads the type the handle is.

Round 2965.decision_summary:
ZA-3517, a consumer's claim that wz_dissect.h and the library disagree about the field document. The header said a document asked for without a selector carries no "selected" key, and that the SUBSUMED mark on the older field doors meant the selector door answers their question and one more. The consumer swapped an older door for wz_dissect_pcap_fields_where_limited with an empty selector and its golden moved on every row.

The claim was right, and read from the code rather than from the ticket. An empty selector parses to Filter::any; fields_json_where always passed the row verdicts through, so every row carried a word, yes for a judged row and unjudged for the rest. The behaviour was not an accident: the document-revision gate rendered the selector door with the empty selector precisely to measure the four words. What was wrong was the header sentence and the reading it invited.

The choice was between making an empty selector write no verdict, and leaving the code and correcting the header. The first is taken, for four reasons. The ABI states in three places that an empty selector is the identity, for the census doors, where it is literally the older document; the field family was the one exception and nothing said so. The header's own advice for a SUBSUMED door is that new code should reach for the successor, which is only safe if the successor can say what the old door said. The one consumer read the empty selector as "do not narrow" and reads no verdict from that call. And the only wz-side reader of a verdict under an empty selector was the revision gate, which now asks with bytes >= 0, the weakest selector the language has.

No revision of the field document moved. Its key set, its four-word vocabulary and its carries are unchanged; what moved is the condition under which the key is written, to what the header always said. The residue: a consumer that read selected under an empty selector now finds it absent. None is known.

The root cause is the part worth keeping. capi_header_subsumption.py holds the header's SUBSUMED lines against the library's doors axis and holds nothing else, so the mark was true of this door for as long as it was written and the claim a reader took from it was not, and nothing could tell. The census family has had byte-identity tests for its subsumed doors since R311y887; the field family had them for the doors joined by fields_limited and never for the door that joined those. The repair is a witness per SUBSUMED door whose population is derived from the walk the library itself reports, not a list.

Round 2966.decision_summary:
ZA-3509, a consumer's performance claim about wz_dissect_live_fields_where. A consumer narrowing a message list with a selector needs, per row, the four coordinates that join the row to a record and the word the selector said. The only door that gave it rendered every row's whole tree, carried state and session verdicts beside those five values. The consumer measured it on a synthetic capture of 25,360 rows: 171 ms for the door, a 58 MB document, 1.5 s to read it, paid on every chip toggle, against the 0.1 to 0.2 s of the evaluator it had retired in favour of this library's. Those numbers are the consumer's; this round did not reproduce them.

The ask left two shapes open: a light document on the same handle, or a "no tree" argument on the existing door. A new door and a new document are taken. An argument would give one name two document shapes, so every reader of the tree would have to reason about a document that sometimes has none; a new symbol is what capi_abi_pin.py watches and what a revision number can announce. The existing door's signature is published and is not touched.

The renderer choice is the load-bearing one. The light document is not a second traversal that must be kept equal by discipline. Its verdict comes from row_verdict_of, hoisted out of the field document's own renderer in the previous round and called by both; its coordinates come from the same numbering; and a test holds every row of the field document to appearing in the light one, in order, with the same word, over every fixture capture and several selectors.

Its rows differ from the field document's in two ways, both that document's limitation. The field document renders a datagram row only when it can re-read the packet from the capture container and the second read agrees; the verdict needs no packet, so this door has a row for every frame the dissection framed and takes no container. A handle fed by push, which has no container, therefore gets datagram verdicts it could not get before. And neither renders a recovered QUIC stream or a serial line. The choice not to mirror the container dependency is what lets the door drop the bytes argument, the declarations argument and the row cap at once: the verdict does not depend on how a payload is decoded, and a cap trims trees this document does not have.

An empty selector is the identity here as everywhere: rows and coordinates, no verdict. The door could have read an empty selector as "everything matches" and answered yes throughout, which would have made it the one door where no selector and the selector that matches all differ.

Measured through the built release library, over the real ABI, on synthetic captures of one TCP flow whose segments carry five KeepAlives each. Both doors list the same rows at every size and both scale linearly. At 25,360 rows the light document is 2.10 MB against 17.37 MB, the door answers in 3.6 ms against 40.5 ms, and parsing takes 12.5 ms against 155.5 ms. These rows are the smallest a row can be, so the ratio understates what the consumer's real rows will show.

Round 2968.decision_summary: Round 2968 measures what the zenoh-pico drop-in puts on the wire as a PEER, beside a peer and beside a router, against the real libzenohpico, and closes the one part of the difference that a program could observe. The differential had compared the client arm only, so the three things a peer's mode changes were unmeasured: whether it asks, how it asks, and how it retracts. Measured, wz matched the real library on the first two and differed on the third: a pico peer names the key it holds when it retracts a subscriber or a queryable (`_z_undeclare_subscriber` and `_z_undeclare_queryable` attach `_z_declared_keyexpr_alias_to_wire` in every mode but client) and wz retracted by id alone. That is now the runtime's option, set by the pico ABI for a non-client session, and the key it names is the entity's own, which for a subscriber is the prefix declaration and not the key the subscriber was announced on. Two differences remain and are pinned from both sides rather than reproduced, on one ground: both are upstream doing something no program can see, and copying either would copy a defect. A pico peer's write filter is opened by any matching declaration the session already holds, of either kind, because `_z_interest_replay_declare` replays without regard to what the filter counts and a peer's interest is not aggregate; so pico sends a Query that nothing can answer where wz, as zenoh does, opens a querier's filter on queryables only. And a pico peer that asked a router never sends `Interest(Final)` for its entity interests, so the router keeps them until the session closes, where wz retracts them. The router arm needed a provider node behind the router, because a router announces what another face declared and hosts no entities of its own; without it both arms sent no Query and the leg measured only Interest bits. A finding about the harness, registered as item 848 rather than repaired here: the demo freshness guard walks every non-dev crate, so an edit to one the demo does not link leaves the binary older than a source that cannot affect it, and the remedy the guard prints, a rebuild, does not relink.

Round 2971.decision_summary: Round 2971 builds the first layer of runtime-zero-copy's declared F, chosen by re-measuring the atom rather than by its reason. F says the sample lives in the pool slot, and on no path did it: the sample a subscriber is handed carries an owned payload vector, so the reason's claim that the reassembled message is exactly F held only as far as the decode. Measured along the receive path there were three copies: the link copied each completed frame out of its own buffer, the batch parse projects every message into an owned NetworkMessage, and the subscriber registry copies the payload into the sample. The first is the one with no structure under it, because an inbound frame could only be an owned vector, and it is the base the other two sit on, so it is this round's. RxFrame now carries RxBytes, owned or a range of storage the link lent, which is upstream's ZSlice (an Arc on the storage plus a range) behind an AP-only session-core feature, since the MCU profiles are Arc-free and hand their frames up owned. Every AP read that had a buffer of its own now hands that buffer up instead of copying out of it: the framing read in both arenas, the uring reactor's completions, and the QUIC datagram link. The population was derived from every RxFrame construction in the crates and classified; the two MCU copy sites, zephyr and lwip, are outside this AP-only feature. The atom stays PARTIAL, its reason now names the two remaining copies at their layer, and REMAINING stays 6.

The door is linear in the packet's number: it reads the header of every record before the packet and copies none. A consumer asking for many packets of one large container should keep the frames it already has. An index inside a handle would remove the cost and would be a retention the consumer declined; it is not built.
Growth is held for every prefix of two synthetic containers. A real growing file being followed by the consumer is the case those tests cannot reach, and the consumer's own rerun is the measurement.

Decoding the capture framing in the consumer would have been a second decoder. wz_dissect_pcap_frame_bytes (ABI 21) hands a packet out of the capture container by the number the row names, as an owned copy in a buffer the caller sized, link header included, under the ask-the-size rule of wz_dissect_live_message_bytes. It takes the container and not a handle: a handle keeps no captured frame, and giving it one would mean a retention policy or a Retired answer for most packets; the consumer holds the container and asked for neither. The pcap and pcapng walks now lend packet bytes and let their sink stop, and the follow door and the new door run ONE walk, so the two numbers come from the same code.

verification_bullets: On a build machine: every test target of wz-capture, wz-analyze, wz-capi-dissect, wz-tls-record, wz-replay and wz-capi-replay passes, with wz-capture at its dissect and fixtures features and wz-integration-tests type-checked against them; clippy with warnings denied is clean for the three changed crates at both feature sets; lanes C1bo (ABI 22, 32 symbols, the C consumer reads revision 19 and calls the new door) and C1bz pass.

The row promise was measured before it was written. Eight scenarios read a capture one packet at a time and compared every row two successive documents both held, matched by seq, cell by cell; each scenario's set of changed cells is pinned exactly. Next is the read task, and its design is derived, not guessed. pico spawns its keep-alive, lease, read and accept tasks onto a background executor at open and starts the executor only if auto_start_read_task is set (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/api/api.c, z_open); zp_stop_read_task stops it and zp_start_read_task starts it, both idempotent, and zp_read_task_is_running answers the started flag (vendor/zenoh-pico/src/runtime/background_executor.c). In wz every role's faces are driven inside ONE future on the session's drive thread (crates/wz-capi-core/src/drive.rs, open_blocking's block_on; the accept loop holds every accepted face in one FuturesUnordered), so the seam is ONE gate: an adapter that does not poll that future while the read task is stopped and polls it while the session is closing, armed at the three open-success signals (drive_dial's on_up, drive_peer's start window, drive_listen's bind) and followed by a yield so frames already in the socket are not processed in the same poll. SessionState gains start, stop and is_running, close() must wake the gate, and OpenStance gains whether the read task starts (zenoh-c passes true). The writers are spawned tasks and keep running, which matches pico's z_put writing on the caller's thread.

Measure it the way this round measured the options: a compile-twice driver that opens a listening session with auto_start_read_task false, has a wz-ap-demo dial in and publish, declares its subscriber, starts the read task, and prints zp_read_task_is_running at every step, stops and starts it once more; its reference arm must show the traffic held until the start, and the reason's STILL LIVE line and the gate's auto_start_read_task entry come out in the same commit. Controls: the gate never armed, never woken by close (the join must hang and the test time out by name), the yield removed.

The real function is one line over zenoh's own Display for the id, so it now calls the workspace's one recipe for that spelling.
